bottlenecks.name: Perturbation robustness collapse (camera viewpoint & robot init-state worst)
bottlenecks.evidence: LIBERO-Plus (10,030 tasks, 7 perturbation dims, L1-L5 difficulty) on 10 VLAs: overall 95%→<30% under modest perturbations. Camera viewpoint is the single worst factor: OpenVLA 76.5%→1.1% (-75.4pt), UniVLA 95.2%→4.3% (-90.9pt), Nora 87.9%→4.0% (-83.9pt). Robot initial-state: pi0 94.2%→6.6% (-87.6pt), OpenVLA-OFT_w 95.3%→43.7% (-51.6pt). Object layout milder: OpenVLA 76.5%→31.6% (-44.9pt), Nora 87.9%→63.9% (-24.0pt). Independently corroborated by LIBERO-PRO: models >90% under standard LIBERO collapse to 0.0% under a generalized-perturbation setting, exposing reliance on rote memorization of action sequences/layouts rather than task understanding.
bottlenecks.severity: high — largest, most consistently reproduced effect size in the literature (up to -91pt); directly matches project's own robustness target dimension and is not on the killed-directions list

bottlenecks.name: Long-horizon task degradation
bottlenecks.evidence: SmolVLA (450M) scores 71% (self-reported, arXiv:2506.01844) / 49.0% (this project's own 100-rollout reproduction, seed 1000) on LIBERO-Long vs OpenVLA-OFT-7B 97.1% and pi0 85.2-94.2% on LIBERO-Long specifically (2511.11298-cited benchmarking context). A ~23-46pt gap that scales with chunk/horizon length rather than task complexity per se.
bottlenecks.severity: high — the sharpest discriminative axis at sub-500M scale per the project's own target dimensions; standard LIBERO average is saturated (94-99%) so this is the only success-rate axis with headroom left

bottlenecks.name: Catastrophic forgetting of VLM semantic/reasoning capabilities during action fine-tuning
bottlenecks.evidence: Fine-tuning a VLM into a VLA on action data collapses general vision-language benchmarks: OpenVLA-7B vs its Prismatic VLM backbone — MMStar 38.8%→0% (-38.8pt), TextVQA 42.5%→0% (-42.5pt), DocVQA 17.5%→0% (-17.5pt), MMMU 35.0%→26.3% (-8.7pt). ECoT-7B: MMB-en 66.2%→3.7% (-62.5pt), MMB-cn 55.7%→4.1% (-51.6pt). Attributed to distribution mismatch between internet-scale VLM pretraining and narrow robot-action fine-tuning data overwriting semantic alignment.
bottlenecks.severity: high — directly threatens generalization/instruction-following, matters to reviewers, and is distinct from the killed 'unfreeze + anti-collapse' direction (that was about frozen-feature information content, R^2=0.75; this is about semantic/VQA capability loss under full fine-tuning, which the project's frozen-backbone constraint already avoids by construction — worth citing as the reason the frozen-backbone constraint is well-motivated)

bottlenecks.name: Language-grounding shortcut / instruction ignorance
bottlenecks.evidence: LIBERO-Plus: models are 'largely insensitive to language variations... tend to ignore language instructions completely' — apparent robustness to paraphrase is actually failure to use language at all; models keep executing the original target action even when the instruction explicitly changes target object. ProGAL-VLA quantifies this directly: raises LIBERO-Plus robustness under robot perturbations from 30.3%→71.5% and 'reduces language ignorance by 3x-4x' by adding explicit grounded-goal verification. RoVLA independently targets the same failure mode with an 'Instructional Consistency' loss term on LIBERO-Plus.
bottlenecks.severity: medium-high — named independently by 3 recent papers (satisfies the '>=2 surveys' bar), not covered by any killed direction or crowded area in the brief, and is a distinct failure mode from generic perturbation robustness (it's a vision-action shortcut bypassing language conditioning entirely, not a perception/pose sensitivity issue)

bottlenecks.name: Inference latency / control frequency dominated by the frozen backbone
bottlenecks.evidence: RT-2 (55B): ~3Hz. OpenVLA (7B): ~5Hz. pi0 (3B, flow matching): ~10Hz. SmolVLA variants (0.24B/0.45B/2.25B) reach 15-30Hz on an RTX 4090 (non-arXiv source, roboticscenter.ai — flag as lower-confidence). Efficient-VLA survey states plainly: 'most latency comes from the language-model component,' motivating lighter-LM research; BitVLA quantization cuts OpenVLA memory 15.1GB→1.4GB without touching the latency-dominant compute path.
citations: roboticscenter.ai (SmolVLA Hz figure, non-arXiv, lower confidence)
bottlenecks.severity: medium — the bottleneck is real (backbone cost dominates, 3-10Hz on 3-55B models) but the brief's crowded-areas list explicitly rejects the standard fixes (quantization, early-exit, KV-cache reuse, speculative decoding), so this axis has little room left for a genuinely novel angle without re-treading crowded ground

bottlenecks.name: Few-shot / low-data adaptation — largely uncharacterized under a fixed protocol
bottlenecks.evidence: No paper found reporting a clean, controlled 10-shot or 25-shot LIBERO number for a single sub-500M checkpoint. Adjacent data points: RIPT-VLA (5-shot, 5 demos/task) improves QueST by +21.2 on LIBERO-Long and +12.4 on ML45 over the SFT-only baseline via interactive post-training (RL-style), implying the SFT few-shot floor is far below full-data performance. pi_RL: few-shot pi0 SFT baseline only 57.6% avg (RL fine-tuning lifts it to 96.1-97.6%); few-shot pi0.5 SFT is 77.1% avg but craters to 43.9% specifically on Long tasks (RL recovers to 94.0%) — i.e., the few-shot deficit compounds with the long-horizon deficit.
bottlenecks.severity: medium — real and confirmed-uncharacterized gap (matches the brief's framing exactly), but existing evidence only comes bundled with RL post-training papers, not a controlled data-efficiency study — any sweep here needs its own clean baseline first, not a repurposed number from an RL paper

bottlenecks.name: Sim-to-real / real-world generalization to novel objects
bottlenecks.evidence: Real-robot ALOHA-Mobile household-task study: pi0 drops from in-distribution 83%→73% (Put Sponge in Pot, unseen instances, -10pt) and 87%→81% (Clean Dish, unseen objects, -6pt) — smaller drop than sim-only perturbation studies but still consistent direction. Failure taxonomy across models: pre-grasp/grasp errors dominate at 32% of failures, release/placement timing 18%, trajectory drift under occlusion 15% — 'most failures stem from low-level geometric or temporal inaccuracies rather than high-level semantic misinterpretation,' i.e. the bottleneck is control precision, not language/scene understanding.
citations: arXiv:2511.11298 (Experiences from Benchmarking VLA Models for Robotic Manipulation)
bottlenecks.severity: low-medium for this project (sim-only per the brief) but worth a sentence for reviewer framing — the failure-mode taxonomy (geometric/temporal >> semantic) is a useful sanity check against over-claiming that a language/semantic fix would close the real-world gap

candidates.name: RND Novelty Gate for Adaptive Test-Time Compute
candidates.mechanism: Attach a Random Network Distillation pair (frozen random target MLP + trained predictor MLP) on frozen SmolVLA backbone embeddings, trained purely self-supervised on in-distribution LIBERO training states (no reward, no labels). At test time the predictor's error against the random target is a per-step OOD/novelty score; when it exceeds a calibrated threshold (LIBERO-Plus-style perturbation), the policy adaptively spends extra test-time compute (invokes an MPPI/BoN fallback) only on flagged steps, staying cheap everywhere else.
source_papers: arXiv:1810.12894 (Burda, Edwards, Storkey, Klimov, Exploration by Random Network Distillation)
arXiv:2602.12375 (Value Bonuses using Ensemble Errors)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus perturbations, and compute efficiency (adaptive test-time compute allocation)
candidates.mechanistic_story: RND's error signal is a purely self-supervised measure of 'have I seen states like this during training.' Since LIBERO-Plus perturbations by construction push the policy off its training distribution, RND error should spike specifically on the perturbation factors (viewpoint, init-state) flagged as worst — a cheap, label-free trigger for spending extra compute only where needed. RND predicts a frozen random function of the CURRENT state (not future dynamics), so it stays outside the world-model exclusion.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: MG-Select's masking-based self-confidence metric is the closest mechanism found but is a dropout-based epistemic-uncertainty proxy used for best-of-N SELECTION, not a trained novelty predictor against a frozen random target used for compute-budget GATING. No RND/prediction-error novelty-detection work found on a frozen VLA backbone.
candidates.integration_path: Two small MLPs (~1-2M params each, one frozen-random, one trained) on frozen SmolVLA backbone features; trained once self-supervised on LIBERO (a few GPU-hours). At inference one extra tiny forward pass per step computes novelty and gates whether to invoke the optional MPPI/BoN fallback.
candidates.pre_flag: OOD-monitor/escalation cluster (C1/C3/C2/C24/C15): competing detectors for the same gate-a-fallback slot — audit picks the winner.

candidates.name: Neural Contraction Certificate for Action-Chunk Verification
candidates.mechanism: Train a small auxiliary head (MLP over pooled VLM features + proprioceptive state, a few M params) that outputs a learned contraction metric M(s) via a Lipschitz/NSD-regularized loss on pairs of nearby executed trajectories, so trajectory pairs under the frozen policy provably converge when M's contraction condition holds. Used two ways with zero backbone gradients: (a) training-free reranker over K sampled flow-matching chunks (keep best contraction margin, no learned reward model); (b) a continuous robustness score flagged low when nearby perturbed states are predicted to diverge.
source_papers: Lohmiller & Slotine, Automatica 1998 (contraction analysis, foundational)
Singh, Majumdar, Slotine, Pavone, ICRA 2017 (CCM robust motion planning)
arXiv 2309.07443 (Sharma, Zhao, Hovakimyan, Learning Tube-Certified Control Using Robust Contraction Metrics)
Dawson, Gao, Fan, IEEE T-RO 2022 (survey of neural certificate methods)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus (viewpoint/init-state) and the lack of any formal (non-empirical) signal for when a chunk is about to fail
candidates.mechanistic_story: Cosine-similarity/uncentered-variance collapse metrics were ruled out by this project's own integrity rules; a contraction metric is a formally-grounded, fundamentally different quantity — it measures whether the local closed-loop Jacobian of (state, chunk) pairs is contracting, not representation variance. Trained on trajectory-pair geometry rather than task reward, it needs no extra labels, and its score is a certified (not merely correlated) stability margin, directly explaining LIBERO-Plus's viewpoint/init-state failure as loss of local contraction.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: arXiv 2603.13782 ('Your VLA Model Already Has Attention Heads For Path Deviation Detection') is the closest — a training-free deviation detector using attention heads for navigation VLAs, but an empirical probe with no stability guarantee, not a certified contraction metric for manipulation chunks. Other hits were non-VLA (ContractionPPO, hydraulic force control, certificate surveys).
candidates.integration_path: Auxiliary head (~1-5M params) trained parallel to SmolVLA's flow-matching expert on existing frozen-backbone features; loss added only to this head. A few hours on 1xA100 using already-collected LIBERO demo rollouts (pairs of nearby trajectories from different seeds/inits). Eval: rerank-by-contraction-margin vs no-rerank on LIBERO-Long and LIBERO-Plus.
candidates.pre_flag: OOD-monitor/escalation cluster (C1/C2/C3/C24/C15).

candidates.name: Quasimetric Progress Monitor for Perturbation Detection
candidates.mechanism: Train a quasimetric embedding d(s,g) — asymmetric, triangle-inequality-respecting — between per-frame frozen-backbone embeddings and the language-instruction embedding, using the QRL objective on successful LIBERO trajectories. At test time monitor d(s_t, g) online: a non-decreasing or spiking distance flags stuck/perturbed execution (LIBERO-Plus viewpoint/init-state shift), triggering a cheap fallback (extra resampling, or hold the last stable chunk instead of extrapolating).
source_papers: arXiv:2304.01203 (Wang, Torralba, Isola, Zhang, Optimal Goal-Reaching RL via Quasimetric Learning)
arXiv:2208.08133 (Metric Residual Networks for Sample-Efficient GCRL)
arXiv:2409.08724 (Quasimetric Value Functions with Dense Rewards)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus perturbations (worst factors: camera viewpoint, robot init-state)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Standard scalar value/critic heads collapse goal-distance and progress into one undifferentiated number. A quasimetric explicitly enforces the triangle-inequality structure provably correct for goal-reaching value functions, giving a principled stuck/regression detector — unlike raw cosine-similarity drift, which this project's own integrity rules flag as unreliable on uncentered activations. It is a distance function, not a dynamics predictor, so outside the world-model exclusion.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Projective Quasimetric Planning / ProQ (arXiv:2506.18847) applies quasimetric sub-goal planning to navigation only, no language conditioning, no manipulation, no frozen-VLA monitoring use. No VLA-paired quasimetric work found.
candidates.integration_path: Small metric-embedding MLP (~1-3M params) on frozen SmolVLA visual+language token features, trained offline via QRL loss on existing LIBERO demo trajectories (under a GPU-day, one-time). Runs as an inference-time monitoring side-channel — one extra tiny forward pass per control step, near-zero added latency.
candidates.pre_flag: OOD-monitor/escalation cluster (C1/C2/C3/C24/C15).

candidates.name: Uncontrolled-Manifold Loss Reweighting
candidates.source_domain: optimal feedback control theory / minimal-intervention principle
candidates.mechanism: Estimate a low-rank, per-timestep task-relevant subspace of each action chunk from demonstrations (a small learned linear projector trained to predict task-completion/goal-state from partial perturbations of the chunk), then reweight SmolVLA's flow-matching regression loss to penalize deviation heavily along the task-relevant subspace and lightly (or not at all) in orthogonal 'uncontrolled' directions, replacing the uniform per-dimension L2 loss.
source_papers: Todorov & Jordan, 'Optimal feedback control as a theory of motor coordination', Nature Neuroscience 2002
Scholz & Schöner, 'The uncontrolled manifold concept', Experimental Brain Research 1999
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness/generalization collapse under LIBERO-Plus init-state perturbation, plus long-horizon capacity wasted matching irrelevant per-step trajectory shape
candidates.mechanistic_story: The minimal-intervention principle and uncontrolled-manifold concept explain why biological reaching is precise in task-relevant coordinates but variable elsewhere: correcting only what affects the goal makes control both robust (redundant DOFs absorb disturbance for free) and generalizable (never overfitting free directions). SmolVLA's uniform flow-matching loss spends equal capacity nailing every action dimension, including nuisance directions that vary freely across LIBERO-Plus init-state perturbations.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: None found applied to a learned VLA or imitation-learning loss. Search hits were the source neuroscience/control literature and a classical robot-arm feedback controller (PMC4940408) with no learned policy and no VLA.
candidates.integration_path: Add a <1M param low-rank relevance projector trained jointly with (but architecturally separate from) the flow-matching expert; it only reweights the training loss matrix, adding zero inference-time latency or parameters once trained. Cheap diagnostic first: check whether the learned relevance subspace concentrates variance on task-relevant action dims on a handful of LIBERO tasks before training a full policy.
candidates.pre_flag: Shares the task-relevant-subspace primitive with C29 (MinIntervene); different lever (training loss vs inference replan gate), kept separate per audit guidance.

candidates.name: Learned Variable-Impedance Action Channel
candidates.mechanism: A small auxiliary head (few hundred K to ~2M params) on frozen backbone pooled features predicts, alongside the existing pose/gripper action, a per-timestep diagonal Cartesian stiffness/damping schedule. The predicted pose target is tracked by a low-level impedance/operational-space controller rather than executed as a hard setpoint. Trained with heuristic supervision (low stiffness around contact/gripper-close events inferred from demo labels, high stiffness during free-space transport) — no reward model, no backbone gradient.
source_papers: Hogan, ASME JDSMC 1985, 'Impedance Control: An Approach to Manipulation' (foundational)
Abu-Dakka & Saveriano, Frontiers in Robotics and AI 2020, 'Variable Impedance Control and Learning — A Review'
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness under perturbation/contact-rich distribution shift and contact-heavy task success (MetaWorld-hard tier)
candidates.mechanistic_story: A frozen backbone's action output is a kinematic target; under perturbation (distractor, small viewpoint-induced position error), rigid position-controlled execution produces excessive contact force or failure even if the predicted pose was only slightly off. Predicting compliance parameters alongside the pose lets the same nominal trajectory tolerate exactly the kind of small geometric error LIBERO-Plus's worst factors inject, without requiring a more accurate pose — orthogonal to action-representation accuracy.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: None found. Searches ('vision language action robot impedance control compliance', 'variable impedance action head learned stiffness') surfaced only pi0.5/pi0/ChatVLA/OpenVLA/CoT-VLA, none predicting stiffness/impedance.
candidates.integration_path: Small MLP head parallel to the flow-matching expert, trained on existing demo data with heuristic stiffness labels; a few hours on 1xA100. Integration risk (flagged honestly): LIBERO/robosuite's default controller is position-based — needs the simulator's operational-space/impedance controller mode enabled; check availability/stability before committing budget.

candidates.name: ECAT — Error-Correcting Action Tokens
candidates.mechanism: Wrap the predicted action chunk in a systematic error-correcting code: the head emits n original values plus r redundant parity coefficients (fixed linear code or a small jointly-trained TurboAE-style encoder/decoder), and a lightweight decoder performs syndrome-style correction on the chunk before dispatch. Backbone untouched; only the head's output layer and the small decoder are trained.
source_papers: Jiang, Kim, Kannan, Oh, Viswanath — Turbo Autoencoder, NeurIPS 2019 (arXiv 1911.03038)
Kim et al. — Communication Algorithms via Deep Learning, ICLR 2018 (arXiv 1805.09317)
Hamming — Error Detecting and Error Correcting Codes, BSTJ 1950
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus (viewpoint/lighting/distractor-induced errors concentrated in a subset of chunk timesteps)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Under visual perturbation the action head rarely fails uniformly across a 50-step chunk — a sparse subset of timesteps get knocked off while the rest stay locally correct, exactly the sparse-error regime channel codes are built for. A systematic code with jointly-trained redundancy lets a cheap decoder recover corrupted timesteps from surviving parity the way a channel decoder recovers bit-flips, without touching perception or the frozen backbone.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: SC-MLLM (arXiv 2405.17418) and RoboFAC do behavioral/semantic self-correction (detect a failure, ask for help/replan) — not information-theoretic redundancy coding. 'The Compression Gap' (arXiv 2604.03191) diagnoses an information bottleneck in action tokenizers but proposes no redundancy fix. No channel-coding parity mechanism for VLA action chunks found.
candidates.integration_path: Modify the flow-matching/L1 output layer to predict n+r values per chunk (systematic-code redundancy). Add a ~1-5M param decoder between head output and the action buffer performing soft correction before dispatch. Both train jointly with the existing action loss within SmolVLA's normal finetune budget (~hours); backbone frozen.

candidates.name: Evidential Camera-Trust Gate
candidates.source_domain: multi-view evidential deep learning / Dempster-Shafer sensor fusion
candidates.mechanism: Add a small per-camera evidential head (2-layer MLP + softplus → Dirichlet evidence vector) on each camera's frozen vision-encoder+connector output (agentview + wrist). Combine per-view evidence via the closed-form Dempster-Shafer/Dirichlet rule before the fused representation reaches the action expert, replacing naive token concatenation. Trained with synthetic single-camera corruption (viewpoint jitter, brightness, occlusion patches one camera at a time) plus the TMC evidential loss, so a corrupted stream is automatically down-weighted at test time.
source_papers: Han, Zhang, Fu, Zhou, 'Trusted Multi-View Classification with Dynamic Evidential Fusion,' arXiv:2204.11423
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus, specifically camera-viewpoint, the single worst-performing factor (~56% for OFT-class models)
candidates.mechanistic_story: A frozen backbone's fixed pooling/concatenation over camera streams cannot detect that one stream (agentview after a viewpoint shift) is corrupted while the other (wrist-cam) is intact; it blends the bad signal in uniformly. An evidential per-view confidence gate, trained to output low evidence under synthetic single-view corruption, discounts the corrupted stream and leans on the intact one — directly targeting the largest measured LIBERO-Plus failure mode.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: 'Viewpoint-Agnostic Manipulation Policies with Strategic Vantage Selection' (arXiv 2506.12261, WebFetch-verified) is STATIC train-time camera-placement selection, not dynamic per-inference trust-weighting of available views. 'LIBERO-Occ' (arXiv 2606.10862) does generative viewpoint imagination, not evidential fusion of existing views.
candidates.integration_path: Insert between SmolVLM2's per-camera output and the point where camera tokens merge before the flow-matching expert. Per camera: one small MLP (~hundreds of K params); 2 cameras in LIBERO. Combination is closed-form (no extra learned params). Trains jointly using cached-feature infra plus live forward passes only for the small head; hours on 1 A100.

candidates.name: DMP-Chunk: Continuous-Phase Attractor Action Head
candidates.source_domain: biology / classical robotics motor control — dynamic movement primitives, central pattern generators
candidates.mechanism: Replace the flow-matching action expert with a per-chunk Dynamic Movement Primitive parameterization: a lightweight head reads the frozen VLM's pooled feature and outputs per-DOF attractor goal, amplitude, and forcing-term basis weights; the timestep sequence is generated by integrating the DMP's canonical spring-damper attractor system. A persistent phase/canonical-system state is carried across chunk boundaries, so chunk N+1 begins exactly where chunk N ended with matched first/second derivatives, and — because the forcing function is phase-normalized and provably converges to the predicted goal from any actual starting state — execution self-corrects under initial-state perturbation.
source_papers: Ijspeert, 'Central pattern generators for locomotion control in animals and robots', Neural Networks 2008
Ijspeert, Nakanishi, Hoffmann, Pastor, Schaal, 'Dynamical Movement Primitives: Learning Attractor Models for Motor Behaviors', Neural Computation 25(2):328-373, 2013
candidates.vla_bottleneck: long-horizon collapse and chunk-boundary jerk (SmolVLA Long 49-71% vs 94%+ OFT) AND robot-initial-state perturbation robustness (~32% for OFT-class, one of LIBERO-Plus's two worst factors)
candidates.mechanistic_story: SmolVLA resamples a fresh flow-matching chunk from noise every ~50 steps with nothing forcing the new chunk's start state/velocity to match the previous one, so long rollouts accumulate discontinuities that compound into drift. A DMP's canonical system is a first-order ODE with a persistent phase variable, so chunk N+1 is initialized from chunk N's terminal state by construction (smoothness/goal-convergence for free). Separately, under init-state perturbation a raw-chunk mapping executes ballistically wrong; a DMP's attractor re-enters the same trained approach shape from any actual initial state, self-correcting during execution rather than compounding error, with no runtime replanning.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: KeyMPs (arXiv 2504.10011, one-shot VLM-guided keypoint sequencing of DMPs) and Language Movement Primitives (arXiv 2602.02839, language-grounding of motion) connect VLMs to DMPs but not as a trained regression head replacing the flow-matching/L1/token head inside a frozen-backbone <500M VLA evaluated on LIBERO/Meta-World for perturbation robustness. DAM-VLA (arXiv 2603.00926) is a mixture-of-heads routing mechanism, not an attractor dynamical system. Distinct from killed #3 (RTC AR-prefix continuation): DMP is a continuous dynamical system, not a discrete-decoding trick.
candidates.integration_path: A 6th arm of the project's action-representation atlas (heads/head_dmp.py, same conditioning interface as head_l1_chunk.py/head_bspline.py). Per DOF: predict ~15-25 basis weights + goal scalar via a small MLP (~50-150K params for 7 DOF). Loss = closed-form locally-weighted-regression fit of DMP weights to demo trajectories plus the standard rollout L1 loss. Canonical/transformation system integrated as a cheap closed-form ODE at inference (no denoising loop). Trains in hours on 1xA100; backbone frozen. Merged from two independent scanner proposals.
candidates.pre_flag: Adjacent to the crowded compact-action-head/tokenizer atlas (BEAST/B-spline). Consolidated from two duplicate raw ideas (long-horizon-smoothness framing + init-state-self-correction framing).

candidates.name: DreamCoder-style Action-Chunk Library Learning
candidates.source_domain: program synthesis / library learning (wake-sleep Bayesian program induction)
candidates.mechanism: Offline-mine SmolVLA's own successful action-chunk rollouts across LIBERO-Long for recurring multi-chunk motifs via DreamCoder's wake-sleep loop: a wake phase searches chunk-sequence decompositions explaining rollouts, a sleep/abstraction phase (E-graph refactoring) compresses recurring sub-sequences into a growing library of K primitives, and a sleep/dreaming phase trains a small recognition/router network on replayed+fantasized examples to predict which primitive applies. Each primitive is a learned conditioning vector injected into the frozen flow-matching expert. At inference a lightweight router retrieves/composes primitives instead of re-synthesizing each subgoal's motion.
source_papers: arXiv:2006.08381 (DreamCoder, Ellis et al., Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 2020)
DreamCoder (Ellis et al., PLDI 2021)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: long-horizon (SmolVLA 49-71% vs 94%+ on LIBERO-Long) and few-shot data efficiency (uncharacterized at 10-25 demos)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Long-horizon failure is largely a compounding-decoding problem: the expert must synthesize every multi-step motion afresh, so errors compound over the ~8-13 chunks LIBERO-Long needs. Library learning converts recurring motion motifs into reusable, already-verified subroutines, shrinking the novel content the sampler must generate per call and letting a new long-horizon task borrow primitives validated on earlier tasks — attacking both the compounding-error mechanism and the few-shot regime.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: PrimitiveVLA (2605.28634), Uni-Skill (2603.02623), SDP use hand-specified/VLM-labeled discrete high-level skills, not bottom-up compression-driven discovery of continuous action-chunk motifs via wake-sleep/E-graph refactoring. DREAM-Chunk (2606.18589) uses a world model to select among sampled chunks (different mechanism). No DreamCoder-style program-library abstraction on VLA action chunks found.
candidates.integration_path: Offline mining pass over cached rollout logs (CPU-cheap). Library = learned embedding table (K~20-50 × d_cond) + router MLP (~2-5M params) on frozen SmolVLM2 features. Router and library trained end-to-end with frozen backbone and frozen (or LoRA) flow-matching expert on LIBERO-Long, <1 day on 1xA100 reusing feature-caching.
candidates.pre_flag: 'dreaming' = program-fantasy replay for the recognition net, NO environment dynamics model — outside the world-model exclusion despite the name.

candidates.name: Successor-Feature Zero-Shot Goal Transfer Head
candidates.source_domain: successor features / generalized policy improvement (transfer RL)
candidates.mechanism: Train a lightweight successor-feature head phi(s,a) on frozen backbone features to predict discounted future occupancy of a small set of interpretable predicate features (object-in-gripper, object-at-target, computed from sim state during offline training). Decouple this from a per-instruction reward-weight vector w(instruction) read off the frozen language embedding via a linear probe. At test time, on a novel instruction/goal composition, w is computed zero-shot and combined with phi via generalized policy improvement to bias/rerank the flow-matching sampler's candidate chunks — no retraining for new goal combinations.
source_papers: arXiv:1606.05312 (Barreto et al., Successor Features for Transfer in RL)
arXiv:2001.04025 (Universal Successor Features)
arXiv:2110.15701 (Successor Feature Representations)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: generalization to unseen instruction/object compositions (LIBERO-Plus) and robustness (novel effective goals under perturbation)
candidates.mechanistic_story: SF+GPI's proven property is instant policy transfer to a new reward/goal via a dot product, with no additional RL — combinatorial instruction generalization 'for free' from one fixed dynamics representation, unlike a monolithic Q-critic that must be retrained whenever the task/goal distribution shifts. SFs are model-free TD expectations (nothing roll-out-able), outside the world-model exclusion.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Guided Action Flow (arXiv:2607.02092) and VGAS (arXiv:2602.07399) train a monolithic scalar critic on frozen VLA features; neither decomposes into a reward-agnostic successor representation plus a goal-weight vector, so neither supports SF-specific zero-shot GPI transfer to a genuinely new instruction without retraining.
candidates.integration_path: Small MLP (~5-10M params) reading frozen final-layer features, trained via TD on predicate features logged during one offline pass over existing demos; w(instruction) is a linear readout off frozen language token embeddings. Used as an additive reranking bias on chunk candidates at inference. Trainable in under a GPU-day on 1xA100.

candidates.name: MPPI Receding-Horizon Soft-Blending of Action Chunks
candidates.mechanism: Replace single-sample (or best-of-N argmax) execution with the MPPI update: draw K samples per re-planning step (free from the model's native stochastic flow-matching sampler), score each with a cheap smoothness/consistency cost (deviation from the previous chunk's still-valid tail, jerk penalty), weight by softmax exp(-cost/lambda), and execute the weighted AVERAGE trajectory rather than a single winner.
source_papers: arXiv:1707.02342 (Williams et al., Information Theoretic MPC)
arXiv:2109.12147 (Trajectory Distribution Control for MPPI via Covariance Steering)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness / trajectory jerk-smoothness and contact-rich task failures from noisy single-sample chunks
candidates.mechanistic_story: A single sampled flow-matching trajectory can be a low-probability tail draw. MPPI's defining trick — soft-weighted averaging across parallel samples via an information-theoretic cost rather than picking one winner — is mechanistically distinct from every VLA test-time method found (argmax/best-of-N selection or gradient guidance through the ODE using a trained critic); none perform path-integral-style soft trajectory blending.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Guided Action Flow (arXiv:2607.02092) steers the flow ODE via gradients from a trained critic; VGAS (arXiv:2602.07399) does best-of-N argmax via a trained Q-Chunk-Former critic. Both require a trained value function and select/steer a single sample; MPPI needs no trained critic (hand-designed smoothness cost) and produces a blended mean.
candidates.integration_path: Wraps the existing flow-matching sampler at inference; K=4-8 parallel samples per step, softmax-weighted average in raw action space. Zero new trainable params for the baseline hand-designed-cost variant, or a ~1M param learned cost head for the improved variant. No retraining for the baseline.
candidates.pre_flag: K-sample aggregation cluster (C11/C22/C23): adjacent to crowded best-of-N/test-time-scaling; per-idea differentiator is the estimator (soft path-integral blend vs robust statistics vs gossip).

candidates.name: Reliability-Weighted Habit/Goal-Directed Blending
candidates.source_domain: cognitive science — habit formation vs goal-directed control
candidates.mechanism: Run two parallel branches off frozen backbone features: a cheap 'habit' branch (low-rank flow head conditioned only on proprioception + previous action chunk, producing long smooth reactive chunks) and the standard 'goal-directed' branch (full vision+language flow-matching expert). A small arbitration head maintains a running reliability estimate of each branch (prediction consistency/error) and blends their predicted velocity fields per step, shifting toward the habit branch when reliable (cheap, robust to visual perturbation) and toward the goal-directed branch when novelty/disagreement is high.
source_papers: Daw, Niv & Dayan 2005, Nature Neuroscience 8, 1704-1711
Viejo et al., bioRxiv 2020.11.24.396630
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse (LIBERO-Plus viewpoint/init-state) and long-horizon stage-transition failures
candidates.mechanistic_story: Daw et al.'s arbitration model shows animals weight a cheap cached (habitual) controller vs an expensive deliberative one by estimated reliability, not a fixed schedule. Under LIBERO-Plus perturbations the vision-conditioned branch's reliability should measurably drop while a proprioception-only habit branch stays stable for well-practiced sub-motions (transport, reach) — arbitrating by measured reliability, not a hand-tuned mix, should recover success specifically on the perturbation axes that collapse hardest.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: No VLA paper found combining reliability-based habit/goal-directed arbitration. Found only VLA uncertainty-for-failure-detection (2606.20754; token-level uncertainty, OpenReview NX0euXAv98) and the neuroscience arbitration literature, never joined.
candidates.integration_path: Low-rank habit head (~10-20M params) parallel to the flow-matching expert, plus a ~1-3M param arbitration/reliability head reading recent per-step prediction-error statistics, outputting a mixing weight applied at the velocity-field level (convex combination of two velocity predictions is well-defined in flow matching). Habit head trains on demo chunks with vision dropped; arbitration head via short supervised/bandit objective. Backbone frozen.
candidates.pre_flag: Distinct from crowded 'dual-system fast/slow VLA' (which arbitrates by compute/latency budget, not measured reliability) and from killed #3 RTC (which smooths chunk boundaries within one decoder).

candidates.name: RD-IB — Rate-Distortion / Multi-View Information Bottleneck Adapter
candidates.mechanism: Insert a small variational information-bottleneck layer between the frozen SmolVLM2 features and the flow-matching expert, trained with a multi-view IB objective (LIBERO's multiple camera streams, or clean/augmented view pairs, as 'views') that keeps only cross-view-shared information and discards view-specific nuisance via an explicit MI Lagrangian (rate-distortion sweep over beta).
source_papers: Alemi, Fischer, Dillon, Murphy — Deep Variational Information Bottleneck, ICLR 2017 (arXiv 1612.00410)
Federici et al. — Multi-View Information Bottleneck, ICLR 2020 (arXiv 2002.07017)
Fan & Li — DRIBO, ICML 2022
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse — camera-viewpoint (worst LIBERO-Plus factor, ~56%), plus lighting/distractor
candidates.mechanistic_story: LIBERO-Plus analysis shows viewpoint/init-state shift, not missing task understanding, drives failure, and this project's own linear probe shows frozen features carry sufficient action-predictive information (R^2=0.75) — so the problem is nuisance (view-specific) information entangled with task-relevant information. A trainable IB adapter squeezes out nuisance channels via a formal rate-distortion tradeoff without altering the frozen backbone.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: DRIBO applies multi-view IB to image-based RL, not VLA, not frozen-backbone imitation, never LIBERO-Plus. No VLA paper found using IB/MIB as a trainable adapter for viewpoint robustness. Distinct from killed #2 (freeze the whole encoder) and killed #7 (VICReg anti-collapse for unfrozen backbone): RD-IB keeps the backbone frozen and adds a compressive layer to discard conceded-present nuisance info.
candidates.integration_path: Small variational bottleneck (mu/sigma heads + reparameterized sample, dim ~64-128) into SmolVLA's connector. Train with existing action loss + beta*I(Z;X_view) using camera views or photometric augmentation as paired-view signal, sweeping beta. ~2-10M new params, fits SmolVLA's ~20h/1xA100 finetune budget.

candidates.name: CBF-QP Chunk-Consistency Safety Filter
candidates.mechanism: Insert a deterministic QP-based filter between the flow-matching head's raw output chunk and the environment: given the raw candidate action and a small set of barrier functions (joint/workspace limits, chunk-to-chunk smoothness bound, gripper pre-shape consistency), solve a per-step QP finding the minimal perturbation satisfying the CBF forward-invariance condition. Tiny QP (a handful of constraints, low-dim action), sub-ms solve; barriers hand-specified or a small learned auxiliary net.
source_papers: Ames et al., ECC 2019, 'Control Barrier Functions: Theory and Applications'
arXiv 2204.00208 (Breeden & Panagou, Predictive CBFs for Online Safety-Critical Control)
arXiv 1909.08045 (Han & Tedrake, ICRA 2019, Local Trajectory Stabilization for Dexterous Manipulation)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus perturbation and chunk-boundary jerk/discontinuity
candidates.mechanistic_story: When a shifted viewpoint/init-state pushes the backbone off-distribution, the resulting chunk can violate basic physical consistency (large boundary discontinuity, joint-limit excursions, premature gripper closure) even when high-level intent is roughly right. A CBF-QP filter catches these with a formal forward-invariance guarantee and minimal-intervention correction — a hard bound, not statistical smoothing — at negligible latency since the QP is on the low-dim action space.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: None found on VLA + CBF safety filtering (all hits were general CBF control-theory). Distinct from crowded test-time-scaling/verifiers (RoboMonkey, MG-Select, RoVer): those are stochastic best-of-N rerankers using a learned reward; this is a deterministic constraint-projection filter with a formal invariance guarantee applied to every chunk.
candidates.integration_path: Small QP solve (cvxpy/qpOASES) inserted in the lerobot eval loop between action-head output and env.step. Barriers start hand-specified (joint limits, max chunk-boundary delta), with an optional ~1M param learned barrier head as follow-up. Fully inference-time; testable on LIBERO-Plus within a day or two.

candidates.name: Self/Nonself Gate: Negative-Selection Anomaly Detector for Perturbation-Triggered Escalation
candidates.mechanism: Run Forrest et al.'s negative-selection algorithm on frozen VLM pooled features from successful training rollouts ('self'): generate random detector regions in feature space, censor any overlapping self, keep survivors as an unsupervised anomaly detector (zero labeled failures needed). At inference, if the current observation triggers a surviving detector, the policy escalates (extra denoising steps, a slower controller, or a verifier call) instead of executing the fast default path.
source_papers: Forrest, Perelson, Allen, Cherukuri, 'Self-Nonself Discrimination in a Computer', IEEE Symp. Security & Privacy 1994
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus perturbations (viewpoint, init-state, lighting, distractors)
candidates.mechanistic_story: LIBERO-Plus failures concentrate in observations that look subtly different from training but get processed by the same frozen features. Negative selection gives a label-free flag: detectors grown only from successful-rollout 'self' are dense where training coverage was dense and sparse where it wasn't — coverage gaps ARE unlabeled distribution shift, which the algorithm was built to catch with zero examples of the shift.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: None for VLA. Closest is pre-deep-learning robotics fault-tolerance (artificial-immune-system anomaly detection on raw sensor time series), not visual/language distribution shift in a frozen VLM's embedding space. Distinct from crowded verifiers (RoboMonkey/MG-Select/RoVer) which score candidate ACTIONS with a learned reward; this flags anomalous OBSERVATIONS unsupervised and could gate when those verifiers run.
candidates.integration_path: Offline: negative selection once over frozen pooled features from successful rollouts → fixed detector bank in a ~32-64-dim learned projection (a few thousand params for the projection; detector bank non-parametric). Online: single nearest-detector lookup per step (ANN-indexable) gates escalate/don't. No backbone gradients; composes with a fast default head.
candidates.pre_flag: OOD-monitor/escalation cluster (C1/C2/C3/C24/C15).

candidates.name: Algorithmically-Aligned Subgoal-Queue GNN for Length-Generalizing Long-Horizon Execution
candidates.source_domain: neural algorithmic reasoning / GNN message passing
candidates.mechanism: Parse each instruction into a short symbolic subgoal list (cheap in-context parse, no new modality). Train a tiny GNN (2-4 message-passing layers, <5M params) to imitate a 'pop-when-done' queue-execution algorithm over that list, using algorithmic supervision on synthetic subgoal-queue traces (generated offline, decoupled from real LIBERO). Its current-subgoal output becomes the conditioning token fed to the frozen flow-matching expert for the next chunk.
source_papers: Veličković et al., Neural Execution of Graph Algorithms (arXiv:1910.10593, ICLR 2020)
Xu et al., What Can Neural Networks Reason About? (ICLR 2020, algorithmic alignment theory)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: long-horizon, framed as length/order generalization (SmolVLA Long 71 vs OFT-7B 94.5; reproduces at 49% here)
candidates.mechanistic_story: A flat Transformer/flow-matching conditioning stack has no structural bias toward executing a variable-length ordered list correctly. A GNN trained to imitate a queue-pop algorithm is structurally aligned with the actual computation, so per algorithmic-alignment theory it needs exponentially less data to generalize OOD on list length/ordering — directly targeting LIBERO-Long's longer, more-compositional instructions.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Only generic NAR literature (Dudzik et al 'GNNs are Dynamic Programmers', arXiv:2402.13744) and pre-VLA hierarchical scene-graph task planners (arXiv:2012.07277, 2102.13177) using GNNs for symbolic planning, none with algorithmic-alignment/OOD-length framing or VLA/flow-matching integration.
candidates.integration_path: Subgoal parser: reuse the frozen SmolVLM2 generation head in-context or a tiny cached LLM call. GNN queue-executor: <5M params, pretrained ~hours on synthetic algorithmic traces (near-zero GPU), then jointly fine-tuned with the flow-matching conditioning interface on real LIBERO-Long, well within a day.
candidates.pre_flag: Subtask-transition cluster (C25/C20/C16/C46/C40).

candidates.name: Subtask-Indexed Iterative Learning Control (ILC) Correction Buffer
candidates.mechanism: Maintain a lightweight per-subtask feedforward correction term c_k (a low-dimensional vector, not a network) updated online via the classical ILC law c_{k+1} = c_k + L·e_k, where e_k is the tracking error observed the last time this subtask phase executed (within the same episode, or across the k few-shot demo replays) and L is a fixed gain. The correction is added to the VLA's chunk output before execution; backbone and action expert unchanged.
source_papers: Bristow, Tharayil, Alleyne, IEEE CSM 2006, 'A Survey of Iterative Learning Control'
Arimoto, Kawamura, Miyazaki, J. Robotic Systems 1984, 'Bettering Operation of Robots by Learning'
Suresh & Atkeson, 2026, 'Learning Dynamic Rope Manipulation Using Task-Level ILC'
candidates.vla_bottleneck: long-horizon collapse (SmolVLA Long 71% vs OFT-7B 94.5%) and few-shot data efficiency (10-25 demos)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Long-horizon failure in LIBERO-Long is dominated by compounding error across repeated structurally-similar stages (reach-grasp-transport-place), not novel per-stage difficulty. ILC exploits exactly that repetition: instead of the frozen backbone getting every cycle right zero-shot, the policy learns a cheap, provably-converging correction from its own previous attempt at the same subtask type — squarely the low-data regime the report flags, with no additional labeled data or backbone gradient.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Closest is killed self-generated-failure-DPO/recovery (GRAPE 2411.19309, PLD) — but those learn a preference/reward offline and touch policy weights via DPO/RL; ILC is a per-episode, weight-free, deterministic correction law with a classical convergence guarantee, not a learned reward model. Searches surfaced only classical ILC (rope/deformable manipulation), none VLA/frozen-backbone.
candidates.integration_path: No new network. A small stateful wrapper in the lerobot eval loop: a subtask/phase index (gripper-state transitions, or k-means on pooled embeddings) keys a correction-vector buffer; update rule is 3 lines. Testable same-day; only design work is phase segmentation and gain L.
candidates.pre_flag: Pre-flag vs killed #5: no reward/preference model and no policy-weight update — a deterministic classical control law, not DPO/recovery-data learning.

candidates.name: ReservoirAct: Fixed Edge-of-Chaos Reservoir Readout for Near-Zero-Latency Action Decoding
candidates.mechanism: Insert a small, randomly-initialized, entirely untrained recurrent reservoir (echo-state network) between the frozen VLM's per-step pooled feature stream and the action output. Only a linear (or shallow MLP) readout is trained via regression; the reservoir's recurrent weights are fixed and rescaled so the spectral radius sits near 1.0 (edge of chaos), maximizing memory capacity and the separation property.
source_papers: Jaeger, 'The echo state approach to analysing and training recurrent neural networks', GMD Report 148, 2001
Bertschinger & Natschlager, 'Real-Time Computation at the Edge of Chaos in Recurrent Neural Networks', Neural Computation 2004
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency/compute (backbone dominates; iterative flow-matching denoising adds per-step cost) and robustness under LIBERO-Plus
candidates.mechanistic_story: A flow-matching expert needs multiple denoising steps per chunk; a criticality-tuned reservoir replaces that with a single forward pass through fixed random dynamics plus one trained linear readout — the cheapest way to add temporal integration downstream of a frozen backbone. At criticality the reservoir's trajectory-separation property is maximized, pushing perturbed and unperturbed observations that look similar to the backbone further apart in reservoir state space — a plausible lever on LIBERO-Plus's collapse of similar-looking states into wrong actions.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: None found. 'EchoVLA' (arXiv 2511.18112) is a name-only false positive (declarative-memory VLA, unrelated to reservoir computing).
candidates.integration_path: Reservoir: 256-1024 fixed random recurrent units seeded once, rescaled to target spectral radius (zero trainable params). Readout: linear or 2-layer MLP → action-chunk coefficients (~50-300K params). Train standalone as a fast alternate head (compare latency/Hz vs flow-matching) or as a fast default path with the flow-matching expert reserved for gated-anomalous cases. Frozen-backbone compatible.

candidates.name: Two-State Fast/Slow Motor-Adaptation Filter
candidates.mechanism: A ~10-parameter, gradient-free two-rate state-space filter (fast state: high error-sensitivity/low retention; slow state: low sensitivity/high retention, per Smith et al.) applied as an additive corrective bias to the frozen flow-matching expert's output chunk. After each of the first few rollouts in a new setting (new camera pose, object, lighting), the filter updates its two states from observed action-execution error via closed-form linear rules — no optimizer, no gradients.
source_papers: Smith, Ghazizadeh & Shadmehr, 'Interacting adaptive processes with different timescales underlie short-term motor learning', PLoS Biology 2006
candidates.vla_bottleneck: few-shot data efficiency at 10-25 demos, plus robustness to systematic viewpoint/init-state bias
candidates.mechanistic_story: Smith et al. show human adaptation to a systematic sensorimotor perturbation is explained by two superposed linear processes giving rapid initial correction plus stable long-term calibration. A consistent camera-viewpoint shift or new-object-pose offset in LIBERO-Plus is structurally the same systematic bias their model corrects in a handful of trials, directly targeting the 10-25 demo few-shot regime. Learns no dynamics — a closed-form bias filter, outside the world-model exclusion.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: On-the-Fly VLA Adaptation via Test-Time RL (arXiv 2601.06748) and RobustVLA (arXiv 2511.01331) adapt VLAs online but via gradient-based RL/fine-tuning of weights — a different mechanism class from a closed-form, gradient-free two-rate bias filter that never touches a weight.
candidates.integration_path: Stateless-between-episodes, ~10-parameter post-hoc corrector wrapping the flow-matching output in the inference loop; update rules run in microseconds. Pre-registered success criterion: k-shot (k=1,3,5) success on held-out LIBERO-Plus viewpoint/init-state, filter on vs off, same seeds — essentially free (no training run).

candidates.name: Funnel-Gated Re-Inference (adaptive chunk horizon via prescribed-performance control)
candidates.mechanism: Wrap execution in a funnel-control monitor: define a scalar/low-dim tracking error e(t) (predicted-vs-realized end-effector pose from the last chunk, from proprioception) and a time-varying funnel boundary phi(t) that starts wide and decays. While e(t) stays inside phi(t), keep executing the current open-loop chunk (skip backbone passes); when e(t) approaches the boundary, force early re-inference. No neural net — a model-free high-gain feedback law used only as a re-trigger.
source_papers: arXiv 2302.01754 (Berger et al., robust funnel MPC)
arXiv 2310.15544 (Berger et al., funnel control with internal models)
arXiv 2602.22458 (Dennstädt thesis, funnel MPC)
Bechlioulis & Rovithakis, IEEE TAC 2008 (prescribed performance control, foundational)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency/compute (backbone dominates) and long-horizon drift (fixed-schedule re-inference lets error accumulate silently)
candidates.mechanistic_story: The funnel gives a formal, monotonically-tightening bound on allowable tracking error instead of a fixed re-plan interval. On easy rollouts the funnel lets the policy run the backbone far less often (cutting compute/latency); when a perturbation pushes the trajectory off nominal, the funnel catches it early — before it compounds into a chunk-boundary failure — and forces a fresh VLM call.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Closest is killed #3 (continuation-conditioned/RTC AR decoding, 2512.05964, 2606.13355) — but RTC changes the decoder architecture/training; funnel-gating is a training-free, architecture-agnostic runtime monitor deciding WHEN to call the backbone, applicable to flow-matching/L1/AR heads unmodified.
candidates.integration_path: Near-zero-parameter wrapper in lerobot's rollout loop around select_action/chunk-execution: track a scalar error from proprioception, compare to a hand-set/tuned funnel schedule, short-circuit into an early backbone call when breached. Only 2-3 funnel hyperparameters to tune; inference-only, testable in under a day.
candidates.pre_flag: Replan-cadence cluster (C20/C31/C42/C43/C51/C52/C29): adjacent to killed #3 (RTC) and crowded adaptive-chunking (DVAC, HiPolicy, AAC).

candidates.name: Reconsolidation-Style Associative Memory for Perceptual Robustness
candidates.source_domain: cognitive science — memory reconsolidation / attractor dynamics
candidates.mechanism: A small (~5-10M param) modern-Hopfield/dense-associative-memory layer between the raw per-camera embeddings and the frozen backbone input. Offline, store a compact prototype bank (hundreds-to-thousands of clustered embeddings) of clean training-distribution viewpoint/lighting states. At inference, a perturbed observation undergoes one or two Hopfield pattern-completion steps that pull it toward the nearest stored clean-manifold attractor before the frozen backbone sees it.
source_papers: Hopfield 1982, PNAS 79(8)
Nader, Schafe & LeDoux 2000, Nature 406 (reconsolidation)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus (viewpoint and lighting are the named worst factors)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Reconsolidation theory holds a retrieved memory trace is briefly labile and actively repaired against the current (possibly corrupted) context before use — a correction step, not a static lookup. A frozen backbone has no equivalent: a perturbed view feeds straight through. An attractor-based correction layer actively pulls the perturbed embedding back toward the nearest clean-training attractor before the backbone ever sees it — repairing the input rather than hoping frozen features generalize.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Closest are memory-augmented VLA robustness papers — MAP-VLA (2511.09516), MemoryVLA (2508.19236), SOMA (2603.24060) — and 'When Robots Sleep' (2606.17493). All retrieve/replay stored experience for in-context adaptation or continual-skill stability; none use attractor/Hopfield pattern-completion on the perception embedding itself to correct a single corrupted observation. Distinct from killed #2 (freeze more of the network): this adds an active correction module in front of the frozen backbone.
candidates.integration_path: Dense-associative-memory layer between per-camera embeddings and the frozen connector; prototype bank built once via a forward pass over training rollouts, few learnable params (~5-10M, mostly read/write projection) trained with a reconstruction/contrastive objective on clean-vs-perturbed pairs (synthetic perturbations offline). A few hours on 1xA100.
candidates.pre_flag: Adjacent to crowded memory-module-for-long-horizon area; differentiator is attractor pattern-completion for single-observation correction, not experience replay.

candidates.name: Krum-Act (Byzantine-Robust Action-Chunk Aggregation)
candidates.mechanism: Draw K=5-8 stochastic action-chunk samples from the flow-matching head (different noise seeds, near-free). Instead of averaging or cosine voting, merge with a provably Byzantine-robust estimator — Krum (pick the sample with smallest summed distance to its n-f-1 nearest neighbors) or coordinate-wise trimmed mean — treating each sample as a 'client update' possibly corrupted by visual perturbation.
source_papers: Blanchard et al., 'Machine Learning with Adversaries: Byzantine Tolerant Gradient Descent', NeurIPS 2017 (Krum)
Yin et al., 'Byzantine-Robust Distributed Learning', ICML 2018 (arXiv:1803.01498)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus (viewpoint, lighting, distractors)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Under visual perturbation a fraction of flow-matching samples land in a bad mode while the majority still track correctly — structurally identical to a Byzantine-client scenario. Robust-statistics aggregation with a proven breakdown point recovers the majority signal even under correlated corruption, unlike a heuristic similarity filter that can be fooled if the majority itself drifts.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: VOTE (arXiv 2507.05116) uses cosine-similarity committee voting over historical+current predictions, not a robust-statistics estimator with a formal corruption-tolerance guarantee. Delta is swapping the heuristic filter for Krum/trimmed-mean targeted at correlated OOD corruption.
candidates.integration_path: Post-hoc aggregation after the flow-matching ODE solver returns K samples in modeling_smolvla.py; pairwise L2 + Krum/trimmed-mean selection. Zero trainable params, inference-time, frozen-backbone compatible.
candidates.pre_flag: K-sample aggregation cluster (C11/C22/C23).

candidates.name: GossipVLA (Decentralized Gossip-Consensus Expert Ensemble)
candidates.source_domain: gossip / epidemic algorithms for distributed averaging
candidates.mechanism: Replace the single flow-matching expert with 4-6 much smaller replica decoder heads tapping different frozen SmolVLM2 layers/pooling. At inference, run a fixed few rounds of randomized pairwise gossip averaging (each replica blends its action-chunk estimate with a randomly paired replica, weighted by a learned trust scalar) instead of one centralized vote, converging geometrically to consensus without an O(K^2) centralized comparison.
source_papers: Boyd, Ghosh, Prabhakar, Shah, 'Randomized Gossip Algorithms', IEEE T-IT 52(6), 2006
Demers et al., 'Epidemic Algorithms for Replicated Database Maintenance', PODC 1987
candidates.vla_bottleneck: parameter efficiency and robustness — ensemble-level reliability without one large expert or a centralized full-comparison ensemble
candidates.mechanistic_story: A single small expert is a single point of failure. Many tiny replicas gossiping to consensus is cheaper than one big expert or a centralized vote, and gossip's proven geometric contraction to the network average gives a tunable compute/robustness dial (more rounds = closer to true ensemble consensus) settable per episode.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: VOTE (arXiv 2507.05116) is a single centralized cosine-similarity comparison over one model's own historical rollouts, not a decentralized multi-replica gossip protocol with proven geometric convergence over independently-tapped heads. No VLA work found running multiple lightweight heads through randomized gossip rounds.
candidates.integration_path: Replace the ~100M expert with 4-6 heads of ~5-10M params each tapping different frozen layers, plus a ~1K-param trust-weight vector and a fixed 2-3 round gossip loop over action-chunk embeddings before final decode. Comparable training budget to the current single expert; backbone frozen.
candidates.pre_flag: K-sample aggregation cluster (C11/C22/C23); also adjacent to MoE-VLA framing — differentiator is the decentralized consensus protocol.

candidates.name: Sketch-Bound Guardrail (AQP Confidence Sentinel)
candidates.source_domain: databases — approximate query processing with provable error bounds
candidates.mechanism: Maintain a small streaming sketch (Count-Min/AMS-style, few KB) over recent pooled vision-language features and predicted action-chunk statistics during rollout. Each control step, compute a provable (not learned) confidence interval on how far the current input deviates from the sketch's running in-distribution summary, in O(1) update time and fixed memory. On an out-of-bound flag, trigger a cheap deterministic fallback (shrink executed chunk length / force a re-observe).
source_papers: Cormode & Muthukrishnan, 'Count-Min Sketch', J. Algorithms 2005
Hellerstein, Haas & Wang, 'Online Aggregation', SIGMOD 1997
Agarwal et al., 'BlinkDB', EuroSys 2013
PilotDB, Proc. ACM Manag. Data 2025
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus-style perturbation (viewpoint/init-state/lighting/distractor)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Robustness collapse happens because the frozen backbone silently extrapolates on OOD inputs with no signal that it is doing so; ensemble/verifier uncertainty costs extra forward passes a frozen budget can't spare per step. A sketch gives a worst-case, provable error bound on distributional deviation with O(1) memory/update and zero extra backbone passes, so it runs every step nearly free and gates a cheap fallback exactly when the frozen backbone is least trustworthy.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: General OOD/shift detectors for robot learning exist (arXiv 2106.13703, 2211.09916, action-covariance likelihood-ratio) but all are learned/statistical estimators, not fixed-memory sketch-based provable-bound estimators. A general AQP-for-ML-serving pattern (arXiv 2607.00254) targets LLM/data workflows, not VLA action prediction. No VLA-specific sketch-guardrail found.
candidates.integration_path: A few-KB Count-Min/AMS sketch between the frozen backbone and the flow-matching expert; hashes the pooled feature (or sampled action-chunk mean) into fixed-size counter arrays updated online (no gradients). Calibration pass on existing LIBERO-Long eval rollouts sets the threshold. On breach, a wrapper forces chunk_size down (50→8) for that step. <10K params.
candidates.pre_flag: OOD-monitor/escalation cluster (C1/C2/C3/C24/C15).

candidates.name: Option-Critic Temporal Segmentation for Long-Horizon Re-planning
candidates.mechanism: Add a small option-critic module (meta-controller plus per-option termination head) over the frozen action-expert's hidden-state stream. Instead of a fixed chunk-size-50 clock, the module learns WHEN to terminate the current temporally-extended option (triggering fresh re-conditioning on language+vision) vs continue the in-flight chunk, trained via option-critic policy-gradient on sparse LIBERO-Long task-completion reward — no depth, no 3D pose.
source_papers: arXiv:1609.05140 (Bacon, Harb, Precup, The Option-Critic Architecture)
arXiv:1605.05359 (Option Discovery via Spatio-Temporal Clustering)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: long-horizon (SmolVLA 49-71% vs OFT-7B 94%+ on LIBERO-Long)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Long-horizon failure is largely a credit-assignment/re-planning problem — a flat chunked policy commits to a fixed 50-step horizon regardless of subtask boundaries. A learned termination function lets the controller re-condition exactly at subtask transitions (place-then-pick) instead of on a fixed clock, precisely the empirical motivation for options as temporal abstraction in long-horizon control.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: GHOST (arXiv:2606.10025) is hierarchical but predicts explicit 3D end-effector sub-goals from RGB-D — geometry-dependent, adjacent to killed 3D-injection. LLM-augmented HRL scripts subtasks a priori via an LLM. No hit using the formal option-critic architecture with an RL-trained termination function on frozen VLA latents without geometric supervision.
candidates.integration_path: Small transformer/MLP termination head (~2-5M params) plus option-embedding conditioning added to the action-expert context; trained with option-critic policy gradient on frozen backbone features using LIBERO-Long sparse success reward. A lightweight RL finetune of the small action expert on 1xA100.
candidates.pre_flag: Subtask-transition cluster (C25/C20/C16/C46/C40).

candidates.name: Self-Conditioned Action Flow
candidates.mechanism: During training, with some probability run the action-expert's step with a zeroed 'previous clean-action estimate' channel to get a cheap x0-hat (no gradient), then re-run conditioning additionally on that x0-hat. At inference, each flow step reuses the PREVIOUS step's implicit clean-action estimate (available for free from v=(x-x0)/(1-t)) as extra conditioning — no added NFEs.
source_papers: arXiv:2208.04202 (Chen, Zhang, Hinton, 'Analog Bits: ... Self-Conditioning', ICLR 2023)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: long-horizon collapse (SmolVLA 49-71% vs OFT-7B 94%+ on LIBERO-Long) via reduced per-chunk estimation noise, at zero added inference cost
candidates.mechanistic_story: Standard flow matching predicts velocity purely from the current noisy sample and t, forgetting how earlier steps refined the estimate. Chen et al. show self-conditioning gives a large sample-quality gain at FIXED NFE because the network builds on its own running guess; the effect is largest at high noise, which for an action chunk corresponds to disambiguating the sub-goal before committing to fine motor detail. A better-conditioned per-step estimate reduces per-chunk noise that compounds across a long episode.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Past-Token-Prediction (2505.09561) and Training-Time RTC condition on PAST CHUNK boundaries across the control loop — a different object from the WITHIN-CHUNK running denoising estimate. No VLA paper found reusing the within-trajectory x0-estimate as conditioning.
candidates.integration_path: Modify the action-expert forward pass to accept an extra x0_hat input (zero-init on first call), concatenated with the noisy chunk before cross-attention; train with the standard 50%-probability self-conditioning recipe. Adds a small input-projection (~few hundred K params); same NFE, same data, fits the ~4h/20k-step finetune budget.

candidates.name: Weak-Self Autoguidance
candidates.mechanism: Guide the flow-matching expert with an earlier/undertrained checkpoint of the SAME expert: v_guided = v_good + w·(v_good − v_bad). The 'bad' model is a checkpoint saved ~20% through training, so its errors are correlated with (not orthogonal to) the good model's, concentrated exactly where the good model is still uncertain.
source_papers: arXiv:2406.02507 (Karras et al., 'Guiding a Diffusion Model with a Bad Version of Itself', NeurIPS 2024)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus perturbation (viewpoint/init-state drop models from ~95% to 17-70%)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Existing VLA guidance (ACG, RSS/Stable Language Guidance) extrapolates away from a deliberately degraded signal, which is known to push samples off-manifold when the base prediction is already uncertain — exactly the LIBERO-Plus regime where backbone features go OOD and the model must not overcommit to a confidently-wrong action. Autoguidance was purpose-built to fix this CFG failure mode by using a same-capacity, correlated-error 'bad' model, keeping guided samples closer to the data manifold.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: ACG (2510.22201, guides using an 'incoherent variant', aimed at temporal smoothness) and Stable Language Guidance / RSS (2601.04052, decomposes vision vs language causal contribution). Neither uses an undertrained-checkpoint-as-guide for distribution-shift robustness.
candidates.integration_path: Inference-time on SmolVLA's flow-matching expert: periodically checkpoint during training (disk-only), pick an early checkpoint as v_bad, run two ~100M forward passes per denoising step (backbone features cached/shared once). Zero new trainable params. Testable in hours by modifying the lerobot smolvla sampler loop.

candidates.name: Robustness Sinks (Learned Attention-Sink Tokens for the Action Expert's Cross-Attention)
candidates.mechanism: Concatenate a small fixed set of trainable 'sink' embeddings (position-invariant, no scene content) into the frozen VLM's key/value sequence that the action expert cross-attends to. The sinks are never evicted; they give cross-attention queries a stable, low-information target so no single spurious visual token can absorb a disproportionate share of attention mass.
source_papers: arXiv 2309.17453 (Xiao et al., StreamingLLM)
arXiv 2510.15731 (Attention Sinks in Diffusion Language Models)
arXiv 2604.10098 (Attention Sink in Transformers: A Survey)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness / perturbation collapse — LIBERO-Plus 17-70% drops under viewpoint/lighting/init-state; ViTs form high-norm 'artifact' tokens that hijack attention and move to unpredictable locations under shift
candidates.mechanistic_story: StreamingLLM shows transformers need a reliable, cheap attention outlet or attention quality degrades when the natural sink token is perturbed. Under viewpoint/lighting shift, high-norm background tokens in the frozen encoder move, and cross-attention queries with nowhere safe to send unwanted mass instead lock onto these shifted artifacts, corrupting the pooled context. A dedicated always-present sink caps this failure mode without touching frozen weights.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: RetoVLA (arXiv 2509.21243) repurposes the frozen VLM's EXISTING DINO-style register tokens, feeding their spatial content into the action-planning module for accuracy — a content-reuse mechanism. This injects NEW trainable, content-free sink embeddings purely to bound attention entropy for robustness, not to add spatial information.
candidates.integration_path: Add 4-8 trainable sink embeddings (a few hundred params × embed dim) concatenated to the per-frame K/V sequence exposed to the action expert's cross-attention; no backbone updates, trains jointly with the flow-matching loss.

candidates.name: MinIntervene: Minimal-Intervention Selective-Replanning Controller
candidates.mechanism: Learn a task-relevant vs task-irrelevant subspace split from demo-trajectory covariance (uncontrolled-manifold-style: which state directions predict task success vs vary freely across successful demos). At inference, trigger a new expensive VLM-conditioned replan only when the tracked state's deviation from the committed chunk exceeds a threshold IN THE TASK-RELEVANT SUBSPACE; deviations in task-irrelevant directions (rendering-induced feature jitter) are left uncorrected and the committed chunk keeps executing open-loop.
source_papers: Todorov & Jordan, 'Optimal feedback control as a theory of motor coordination', Nature Neuroscience 2002
Todorov & Jordan, 'A Minimal Intervention Principle for Coordinated Movement', NeurIPS 2002
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency/compute (unnecessary replanning) and robustness (LIBERO-Plus viewpoint/init-state, plus long-horizon jerk from over-frequent re-planning)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Biological motor control corrects only deviations that threaten the task goal, which is why natural reaching shows high variability in task-irrelevant dimensions but converges tightly on task-relevant ones. A VLA that replans on every feature wobble reacts uniformly to noise regardless of task relevance, wasting compute and plausibly causing viewpoint/lighting-triggered failure since those perturbations move features in often-task-irrelevant directions. Gating replanning by a learned task-relevant-error signal targets this by construction.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: arXiv 2510.00037 (killed via its re-render pipeline) characterizes perturbation sensitivity but proposes no inference-time minimal-intervention gate. 'Observing and Controlling Features in VLA' (arXiv 2603.05487) does representation steering, not a task-relevant subspace-gated replanning controller. Distinct from killed #3 (RTC) and killed #4 (re-render consistency): this is an inference-time control-theoretic gate needing no retraining and no re-rendered data.
candidates.integration_path: Offline: PCA/CCA on demo-trajectory deviations vs task-success labels → low-dim task-relevant projection (a few thousand params). Online: project the tracked deviation onto this subspace; above threshold, trigger a fresh backbone forward + replan, else continue open-loop. Only the small projection and threshold are trained/calibrated.
candidates.pre_flag: Replan-cadence cluster (C20/C31/C42/C43/C51/C52/C29). Shares the task-relevant-subspace primitive with C4 (loss reweighting); different lever.

candidates.name: Interval-Gated Guidance
candidates.mechanism: Apply any guidance term in the flow-matching expert (language CFG, ACG's coherence term, or autoguidance) only within a middle window of the denoising ODE, e.g. skip the first ~20% and last ~20% of steps, instead of the constant weight every existing VLA guidance paper uses.
source_papers: arXiv:2404.07724 (Kynkaanniemi et al., 'Applying Guidance in a Limited Interval Improves Sample and Distribution Quality', NeurIPS 2024)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency (2x-cost guided sampling used unconditionally by every existing VLA guidance method) and robustness/success rate (guidance-induced artifacts at trajectory boundaries)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Kynkaanniemi et al. showed guidance is harmful near pure noise (the field is uninformative about which mode will be reached, so guidance amplifies toward the wrong mode) and wasted near the clean sample. For action chunking this predicts two wins: cutting the extra guided forward pass outside the window is a direct NFE/latency reduction, and turning off strong guidance right before the chunk is fully denoised reduces boundary jerk/oversaturation — the instability ACG was built to fix, but ACG applies its correction at every step.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: None found applying a noise-level-dependent on/off guidance schedule to a VLA action expert — ACG (2510.22201), the Neuro-Symbolic Safety Guidance paper (2607.01378), and RSS (2601.04052) all apply their guidance term at every denoising step.
candidates.integration_path: Small change to the SmolVLA/lerobot flow-matching sampler (policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py): wrap whatever guidance term is active in an `if t_low < t < t_high` gate; tune the two scalars on a validation split. No new parameters; no retraining if layered on an existing guidance mechanism. Testable in an afternoon.

candidates.name: Tomasulo Fusion: Renamed-Buffer Out-of-Order Multi-Camera Fusion
candidates.source_domain: out-of-order execution with register renaming and hazard detection
candidates.mechanism: Keep a small per-stream ring buffer where each incoming camera frame gets a version tag ('rename'); a lightweight hazard classifier scores whether the current tuple of stream versions is safe to fuse given their timestamp skew, and if a stream is stale/missing it substitutes the last valid renamed version rather than blocking or fusing garbage — instead of SmolVLA's current barrier-sync of all camera streams before fusion.
source_papers: Tomasulo, R.M. (1967), 'An Efficient Algorithm for Exploiting Multiple Arithmetic Units', IBM J. R&D 11(1):25-33
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under perturbation (LIBERO-Plus 17-70% drops; camera viewpoint and init-state worst; multi-camera async/dropout is a direct instance)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Synchronous-barrier fusion bounds effective robustness by the single worst/slowest sensor at any instant; renaming decouples 'which physical buffer holds the freshest valid reading for this virtual slot' from 'did every physical sensor just fire', so the frozen backbone always gets consumable, hazard-checked input instead of blocking or silently fusing a stale/blank frame — reducing the sharp cliff under viewpoint/occlusion that the killed frozen-encoder direction ruled out at the representation level but not at the input-scheduling level.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Missing-camera robustness is addressed via training-time modality-dropout / disentangled fusion (arXiv:2606.15514) or continuous-time interpolation (Neural CDE, arXiv:2203.08715) — both data/training-objective fixes, not a runtime buffering-and-hazard-detection wrapper compatible with a frozen backbone.
candidates.integration_path: A pre-connector module in the SmolVLA data pipeline: per-camera ring buffers (no learned params) plus a ~2-5M param hazard-classifier MLP trained on LIBERO-Plus perturbation replay (synthetic drop/delay on existing logs) to predict safe-to-fuse vs substitute-last-valid. Input-side wrapper; weights untouched. Under a day on 1xA100.
candidates.pre_flag: Latency-hiding / pipeline-scheduling tag (C31 input-fusion; C48/C51 encoder-scheduling) — systems-scheduling ideas around the frozen backbone.

candidates.name: Value-of-Computation Visual Token Economy
candidates.mechanism: A small (~2-5M param) metareasoning controller between the frozen SigLIP vision tower's per-region/per-camera tokens and the VLM connector estimates, per token/view, a Value-of-Computation = predicted reduction in the flow-matching expert's output uncertainty minus a fixed forwarding cost. Only tokens/views above threshold are forwarded through the frozen backbone; the rest are masked or replaced by a cached summary. Trained with a differentiable top-k/Gumbel-softmax gate plus a REINFORCE cost penalty, using realized action-entropy drop as reward.
source_papers: Lieder & Griffiths 2020, BBS 43:e1
Gershman, Horvitz & Tenenbaum 2015, Science 349(6245)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency/compute (backbone dominates) and robustness under LIBERO-Plus distractors/viewpoint clutter
candidates.mechanistic_story: Resource-rational analysis trades a computation's expected benefit against its cost. Most visual tokens (background, redundant views) carry near-zero VOC for the current action; forwarding them wastes FLOPs and lets task-irrelevant clutter/viewpoint noise leak into the pooled representation the head conditions on — the exact pathway LIBERO-Plus perturbations exploit. Gating to high-VOC regions cuts backbone FLOPs and starves the irrelevant-input pathway.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: No VLA paper found doing VOC-style per-token/per-camera gating on a frozen backbone. Closest are general metareasoning (VOC in MCTS 2002.04335; Rational Metareasoning for LLMs 2410.05563; cloud-robotics attention metareasoning 2505.03587) and DASIP (2511.20906, ODE-solver-depth adaptation) — all adapt a different resource, none gate spatial/camera tokens by an explicit VOC.
candidates.integration_path: Input-side gating MLP over SigLIP patch tokens (or per-camera pooled tokens; SmolVLA ingests up to 3 views) masking tokens before the connector. No backbone/action-expert weights touched. ~2-5M params, trainable in a few hours using cached features plus an offline VOC-regression dataset from existing rollouts.
candidates.pre_flag: Adjacent to crowded early-exit/token-pruning/quantization (DeeR-VLA axis) — must be framed as spatial/camera-region value gating, NOT layer-depth early-exit.

candidates.name: Certified-Margin Action Head (Lipschitz-Constrained)
candidates.mechanism: Constrain the action head's weight matrices to bounded spectral norm (Bjorck orthonormalization / spectral normalization per layer) so the head is provably L-Lipschitz in its backbone-feature input.
