Combined with a direct measurement of the frozen backbone's feature shift under LIBERO-Plus-style perturbations (reusing diag_pooled_variance.py / diag_raw_pixels.py tooling), this gives a certified worst-case bound on how much a perturbed action can differ from the clean action, and lets L be tuned as a training target.
source_papers: 'On Robust RL with Lipschitz-Bounded Policy Networks', arXiv:2405.11432
Shi et al., 'Improve Robustness of RL against Observation Perturbations via l-infinity Lipschitz Policy Networks', arXiv:2312.08751
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus (~95% → 17-70% under viewpoint/lighting/distractor) — the observation-perturbation-robustness setting Lipschitz policies were designed for
candidates.mechanistic_story: Standard action heads have no bound on input-output sensitivity, so an unconstrained head can amplify a small backbone feature perturbation into a large, task-breaking action change — a plausible reason performance falls off a cliff rather than degrading gracefully. Constraining the head's Lipschitz constant caps that amplification by construction: given the measured feature-shift magnitude, the maximum induced action error is bounded, turning 'does the model happen to be robust' into a controllable, measurable training target.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Lipschitz-bounded policy networks are established in observation-perturbation-robust RL (arXiv 2312.08751, 2405.11432) but no VLA-specific application surfaced. Scanner flags this as its weakest-verified spot-check (a dedicated 'VLA Lipschitz action head' search was not separately run) — recommend one targeted search before committing compute.
candidates.integration_path: Replace the action head's final MLP/output layers with spectrally-normalized linear layers — a drop-in for head_l1_chunk.py's MLPResNet, same param count, adds a normalization step at forward/optimizer-step time. No backbone gradients, same training budget. Main new work is instrumenting the perturbation-vs-feature-shift measurement to pick a target L.
candidates.pre_flag: Scanner self-flagged as weakest-verified in its set; run one targeted 'VLA Lipschitz-bounded action head' search before compute.

candidates.name: Action Scratch Registers (Self-Attention Register Tokens Inside the Action Expert)
candidates.mechanism: Add a handful of trainable register tokens to the action expert's OWN self-attention among the 50 action-chunk tokens — a scratch space where the model can write chunk-level plan state (which sub-goal phase the chunk is in) without overloading individual per-timestep action tokens, then discard the registers before the action-decoding head.
source_papers: arXiv 2309.16588 (Darcet et al., Vision Transformers Need Registers)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: long-horizon coherence — SmolVLA 49-71% on LIBERO-Long vs 94%+; action chunks spanning multi-stage tasks need chunk-level state per-timestep tokens aren't suited to carry
candidates.mechanistic_story: Darcet et al. show ViTs repurpose low-informative tokens as scratch pads for global information when none is provided, corrupting those tokens' local features. Giving the action expert's self-attention explicit register slots for chunk-level bookkeeping should prevent it from overloading individual action tokens with global-plan information — the same fix applied to a different token population (action-chunk tokens instead of image patches).
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: RetoVLA (arXiv 2509.21243) reuses the frozen VLM's DISCARDED register tokens, injecting spatial content into the action-planning module. This adds NEW registers inside the trainable action expert's own self-attention over action-chunk tokens, targeting temporal/planning coherence within one chunk — different token source, different attention (self- vs cross-), different bottleneck.
candidates.integration_path: Prepend k learnable register embeddings (k~4-8) to the action-chunk token sequence inside the action expert's self-attention blocks only; drop them before the final flow-matching output projection. k × embed_dim added params; trains with the existing flow-matching loss, no backbone gradients.

candidates.name: VIPER-style Programmatic Distillation of the Subgoal Sequencer
candidates.mechanism: After training, distill only SmolVLA's high-level subgoal-sequencing behavior (which of ~5-10 discrete subgoals to condition on next — not the continuous control) into a compact symbolic decision-list program in a small DSL over frozen-backbone-derived object-presence/gripper-state predicates, via VIPER-style imitation-projected program search (imitate the neural sequencer's choices with a program using DAgger rollouts, then prune/verify). At inference the program replaces a full backbone forward pass at each subgoal transition; the frozen flow-matching expert still handles all low-level control.
source_papers: Verma et al., PIRL, ICML 2018 (arXiv:1804.02477)
Bastani, Pu, Solar-Lezama, VIPER, NeurIPS 2018 (arXiv:1805.08328)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency (backbone forward dominates) and robustness (programmatic policies documented to generalize more reliably OOD than their neural teachers)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Every subgoal transition currently re-invokes the ~450M backbone even though the decision is often a simple function of a handful of discrete predicates (object grasped? drawer open?). VIPER's core finding — a program distilled via imitation-projected search is both faster and more robust to distribution shift than the DNN it was extracted from, because its finite structured hypothesis space cannot overfit to spurious high-dimensional correlations — transfers directly: replacing only the subgoal-selection step cuts redundant backbone calls and should be less brittle to LIBERO-Plus perturbations that don't change the relevant predicates.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: 'Learning Neuro-symbolic Programs for Language-Guided Robotic Manipulation' (arXiv:2211.06652) and ProgramPort (arXiv:2304.13826) compile natural-language instructions directly into programs via a learned parser (synthesis from scratch), not VIPER-style distillation of an already-trained neural policy's behavior into a verifiable program for latency/robustness. No paper found doing imitation-projected programmatic distillation of a VLA's subgoal-sequencing layer.
candidates.integration_path: DSL over ~10-20 frozen-backbone-derived predicates; program search run offline via DAgger rollouts against the trained sequencer as oracle (CPU-bound); at inference the program replaces the backbone-forward subgoal-selection step, leaving the flow-matching expert untouched. Full extraction in hours.
candidates.pre_flag: Pre-flag vs killed #6 (distill-from-RL-teacher): this distills the model's OWN policy into a program (a mechanism/representation change for latency/robustness), NOT compression from an RL-tuned teacher.

candidates.name: MDL-Adapt — MDL-Optimal Plug-in Adapter Capacity Selection
candidates.mechanism: Select the capacity (rank/width/bottleneck-dim) of any frozen-backbone plug-in adapter per task and per demo-count regime by minimizing a prequential (online) two-part MDL codelength — bits to describe the adapter weights plus bits to describe the demos given the adapter — instead of one hand-fixed capacity for every task.
source_papers: Rissanen — Modeling by Shortest Data Description, Automatica 1978
Hinton & van Camp — Keeping Neural Networks Simple ..., COLT 1993
Blier & Ollivier — The Description Length of Deep Learning Models, NeurIPS 2018
candidates.vla_bottleneck: few-shot data efficiency at 10-25 demos, and parameter efficiency of the plug-in module itself
candidates.mechanistic_story: A fixed-capacity adapter sized for the full dataset overfits a 10-demo task; MDL says the codelength-optimal capacity shrinks automatically with available data because a too-large adapter costs more bits to describe than it saves in prediction error. A prequential MDL criterion (codelength training sequentially on demos 1..i and predicting demo i+1, summed) as the capacity-selection rule gives a principled per-task adapter size, shrinking the average deployed adapter.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Generic LLM LoRA rank-sweep studies exist (arXiv 2504.12397) but are not MDL/prequential-codelength-based and not applied to VLA adapters. No VLA paper found selecting adapter/bottleneck capacity via a description-length or prequential criterion tied to the few-shot demo-count regime.
candidates.integration_path: A training-time wrapper around whichever plug-in module the lab ships (e.g. the RD-IB bottleneck, or a LoRA adapter): for each few-shot arm (10/25/50 demos), train a small capacity sweep, compute each one's prequential codelength on the held-out-in-order demo stream, keep the minimum-codelength capacity. No new inference params — a few extra short training runs (~hours total) per task.
candidates.pre_flag: Meta-method that composes with other candidates (e.g. C13); not a standalone contribution on its own.

candidates.name: Retrieved-Anchor Bridge Matching
candidates.mechanism: Replace the action expert's Gaussian-noise-to-action path with a Schrödinger-bridge path between the current (possibly perturbed) prediction and a retrieved reference: k-NN retrieve the nearest training-trajectory state in cached backbone-feature space (one-time FAISS index, no backbone gradient) and its action-chunk continuation, then run a small entropic bridge module (trained via iterative Markovian fitting) that transports toward that anchor with a tunable temperature.
source_papers: arXiv:2303.16852 (Shi, De Bortoli, Campbell, Doucet, 'Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge Matching', NeurIPS 2023)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus, specifically the worst factors (camera viewpoint ~56%, robot init-state ~32%)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Flow matching always starts from an uninformative Gaussian prior; under perturbation the conditioning shifts OOD but the ODE source is blind to it, so the learned velocity field extrapolates confidently into the wrong region. A Schrödinger bridge defines transport between two DATA-side endpoints with entropy-regularized paths, staying closer to the data manifold than a straight-line coupling extrapolated from noise, and supplies an explicit correction signal (the retrieved anchor) exactly when the raw prediction is least trustworthy.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: WarmPrior (2605.13959) uses the PREVIOUS CHUNK's own prediction as a warm-start prior for straightness/inference speed — a within-episode temporal prior aimed at latency, not a retrieved cross-episode anchor aimed at perturbation robustness. No retrieval-conditioned Schrödinger-bridge VLA work found.
candidates.integration_path: New lightweight bridge module (~20-30M params) alongside the flow-matching expert; build the FAISS index once over cached frozen-backbone features (reuses features already computed during training). Train the bridge with DSBM's iterative Markovian fitting on cached-feature/retrieved-anchor pairs. Backbone frozen; trainable in under a day.

candidates.name: Ground-Truth HER Relabeling for Few-Shot Action-Expert Training
candidates.mechanism: For every LIBERO rollout (successful or not, including cheap autonomous/exploratory rollouts), relabel the language instruction in hindsight using the simulator's ground-truth achieved predicate (which object got picked/placed, which state became true) via HER's future/final relabeling. A trajectory that 'failed' instruction A but achieved state B becomes a valid positive (state, hindsight-instruction-B, action-chunk) BC pair. Multiplies the usable training set from a fixed small demo budget without new teleop and without VLM-generated (hallucination-prone) labels.
source_papers: arXiv:1707.01495 (Andrychowicz et al., Hindsight Experience Replay)
arXiv:2102.12962 (Bias-reduced Multi-step HER)
arXiv:2209.13046 (Understanding Hindsight Goal Relabeling as Divergence Minimization)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: few-shot data efficiency at 10-25 demos (largely uncharacterized)
candidates.mechanistic_story: BC starves on scarce demos because every rollout that doesn't match its assigned instruction is discarded. HER's insight is that any trajectory is a perfect demonstration for the goal it actually reached — reusing 'wrong-goal' rollouts as correct demonstrations for a relabeled goal multiplies effective training signal from the same collected data, directly attacking the few-shot gap rather than requiring more teleop. This is a relabeling mechanism, not data scaling.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: CAST (arXiv:2508.13446) uses a VLM to generate counterfactual language labels — the closest hit, but relabels via VLM-generated captions rather than ground-truth simulator state, and is not framed around few-shot data-multiplication or HER's explicit future/final relabeling-ratio schedule.
candidates.integration_path: Pure offline data pipeline over the LIBERO demo + autonomous-rollout buffer; feeds the existing flow-matching BC loss unchanged. Zero new inference params; frozen backbone untouched. A few hours of relabeling plus a normal action-expert finetune.

candidates.name: Denoising-Depth Router (Token-Level Mixture-of-Depths in the Action Expert)
candidates.mechanism: Insert a lightweight top-k router at each self-attention/MLP block of SmolVLA's flow-matching action expert. At every layer the router scores the ~50 action-chunk tokens (conditioned on a learned embedding of the current ODE denoising timestep plus each token's chunk position) and only the top-k fraction get full attention+MLP compute that layer; the rest skip via the residual path, as in Mixture-of-Depths but applied to action tokens conditioned on flow timestep. Trained end-to-end with the flow-matching loss.
source_papers: arXiv 2404.02258 (Raposo et al., Mixture-of-Depths)
arXiv 2412.16822 / CVPR 2025 (Layer- and Timestep-Adaptive Differentiable Token Compression for Efficient Diffusion Transformers)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency (flow-matching requires ~10 sequential integration passes per control step, dominating on-robot control frequency once the VLM cache is reused) and compute efficiency
candidates.mechanistic_story: Early noisy denoising steps mostly fix coarse trajectory shape (low information per token), while late steps need precise per-timestep correction near the immediate control horizon — MoD lets the model learn to spend FLOPs where residual error is largest instead of applying uniform depth to every action token at every step.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: MoLe-VLA (arXiv 2503.20384, Mixture-of-Layers with a spatial-temporal router) does dynamic layer-skipping at whole-layer/whole-backbone granularity on the VLM, not token-level routing inside a frozen-compatible action expert conditioned on flow timestep.
candidates.integration_path: Plug-in router (small MLP + top-k mask) added to each block of the existing action-expert transformer only — no backbone gradients. Router adds well under 1% extra parameters; trainable jointly with the standard flow-matching objective.
candidates.pre_flag: Adjacent to crowded early-exit/MoE-VLA area; differentiator is token-level flow-timestep-conditioned routing inside the action expert.

candidates.name: Execution-Guided Postcondition Verification for Closed-Loop Chunk Replanning
candidates.mechanism: Attach a small GNN 'postcondition checker' over language-grounded object-token nodes (from the frozen backbone's existing 2D patch tokens, no depth) that predicts the expected post-chunk object-relation graph from the pre-chunk graph plus the current chunk's flow-matching conditioning vector. After each real chunk executes, compare predicted vs observed post-chunk graph; a large mismatch injects a discrete 'retry/recover' conditioning token for the next flow-matching call instead of blindly continuing the pre-planned subgoal sequence.
source_papers: Execution-Guided Neural Program Synthesis (Chen, Liu, Song, ICLR 2019, OpenReview H1gfOiAqYm)
Write, Execute, Assess: Program Synthesis with a REPL (arXiv:1906.04604, Ellis et al., NeurIPS 2019)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: long-horizon compounding error and robustness collapse under perturbation (LIBERO-Plus: 95%-models drop to 17-70%, worst factors viewpoint/init-state)
candidates.mechanistic_story: SmolVLA executes chunks open-loop against its own plan; a perturbation-induced state mismatch is invisible to the sampler until it compounds over several chunks. Execution-guided synthesis's insight — condition generation on the actually-observed effect of the previous step, not just its intent — gives a cheap structural verification signal (predicted vs observed object-relation graph) that catches drift at the chunk boundary, before it propagates through the remaining 8-13 chunks.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: 'Recover: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Failure Detection and Recovery' (arXiv:2404.00756) and arXiv:2405.18948 (IROS 2024) use a dense scene-graph transition model + discriminator, but for discrete TAMP-style symbolic re-planning over a hand-built planner, not embedded in a continuous frozen flow-matching VLA's chunk loop, and not at sub-500M scale. This keeps everything differentiable/continuous, triggering a conditioning-token change rather than symbolic re-search.
candidates.integration_path: GNN postcondition checker (~3-8M params, 2-3 message-passing layers) between the frozen backbone and the flow-matching expert; trains on (pre-chunk graph, executed chunk, post-chunk graph) triples mined from existing rollouts, jointly with a learned 'recover' embedding. No backbone/expert gradients for the checker; joint fine-tune of the conditioning interface, <1 day.
candidates.pre_flag: Subtask-transition cluster (C25/C20/C16/C46/C40). Prediction-adjacent (predicts symbolic object-relation graphs, not latent/pixel state) — outside the world-model exclusion; audit may overrule.

candidates.name: Cognitive-Load-Decomposed Chunk Horizon & Replanning
candidates.mechanism: A small (~2-3M param) load estimator reads three separate signals each step: extraneous load (visual-token entropy/clutter from SigLIP features), intrinsic load (multimodality/curvature of the flow-matching velocity field from a few sampled draws), germane load (novelty of the current sub-goal, embedding distance from the last replanning point). These three signals — kept separate rather than collapsed into one difficulty score — set the action-chunk horizon and replanning cadence: long chunks/infrequent replanning during low-load habitual segments, short chunks/frequent replanning at high intrinsic/germane load.
source_papers: Sweller 1988, Cognitive Science 12(2) (intrinsic/extraneous/germane load taxonomy)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: long-horizon collapse (SmolVLA Long 49-71% vs 94%+ for OFT-7B) and latency/compute efficiency
candidates.mechanistic_story: Cognitive load theory decomposes load into causally distinct sources calling for different responses, rather than one scalar difficulty number. SmolVLA's fixed chunk size and cadence apply uniformly regardless of whether the moment is a repetitive low-load transport segment or a high-load stage transition — exactly where LIBERO-Long's gap concentrates. Decomposed-load-driven chunk horizon lets the policy spend its temporal budget where sub-goal structure is actually being constructed and coast through low-load segments cheaply.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: DASIP (2511.20906, NeurIPS 2025) adapts ODE/SDE solver depth per step via a learned difficulty classifier, cutting compute 2.6-4.4x. It uses one scalar difficulty to change per-step integration cost, not three decomposed cognitive-load signals to change the temporal chunk horizon/replanning cadence. Must cite DASIP explicitly.
candidates.integration_path: A control-flow wrapper around the existing action-expert call: the load estimator reads intermediate backbone/flow activations already computed; its outputs (chunk horizon H, replan-trigger) gate how often the rollout loop calls the expert. ~2-3M new params, trained via short supervised regression against realized tracking error and replan-triggered success. <1 day.
candidates.pre_flag: Replan-cadence cluster (C20/C31/C42/C43/C51/C52/C29); cite DASIP as close prior art and argue decomposed-load/chunk-horizon is a different lever than solver-step depth.

candidates.name: Schema-Slot Fast-Binding for Few-Shot Generalization
candidates.source_domain: cognitive science — schema learning / fast mapping
candidates.mechanism: Factor the action expert's conditioning embedding into a 'schema code' (a small learned codebook of ~16-32 reusable motor schemas — pick, place, pour, open, rotate — via vector-quantizing action-chunk trajectories across LIBERO) and a 'slot filler' (an object/pose embedding read from vision via cross-attention). At few-shot adaptation, only the slot-filler pathway updates, via a single fast Hebbian outer-product write into a small key-value memory — no gradient descent, no backbone touch — mirroring one-shot fast mapping.
source_papers: Carey & Bartlett 1978 (fast mapping)
Whittington et al. 2020, Cell 183(5) (Tolman-Eichenbaum Machine, structure/content factorization)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: few-shot data efficiency at 10-25 demos and cross-task/object generalization
candidates.mechanistic_story: Schema theory and the Tolman-Eichenbaum Machine show biological generalization factors a reusable 'structure' code from task-specific 'content', so a new instance only fills its content slot. A flow-matching expert currently entangles both in one conditioning vector, so few-shot adaptation must nudge the whole network. Separating schema (reused, frozen after pretraining) from slot (one-shot, associatively written) lets a new object/goal be bound in a single fast write.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: AnySlot (2604.10432) addresses slot-level object placement but not a schema/content factorization with one-shot Hebbian binding. In-context-learning-for-VLA (TOPIC, CapVector — CLAUDE.md-crowded) uses prompting recipes, not an architectural schema-codebook + associative memory. None found combining fast-mapping one-shot binding with a structure/content-factored action head.
candidates.integration_path: Insert a VQ bottleneck (~1M params codebook) plus a small cross-attention slot reader (~5-10M params) between the frozen backbone output and the flow-matching expert's conditioning; add a small external KV memory written via one Hebbian outer-product per new object/task. Backbone and codebook frozen after pretraining on the full LIBERO suite; only KV memory changes per task (inference-time adaptation).
candidates.pre_flag: Adjacent to crowded in-context-learning-for-VLA (TOPIC/CapVector); differentiator is the architectural schema-codebook + Hebbian associative memory, not prompting.

candidates.name: PRC — Progressive Rate-Distortion (Successive-Refinable) Action Chunking
candidates.mechanism: Add a nested per-step distortion term to the flow-matching training loss that enforces the successive-refinability (Markov) condition across ODE integration steps, so the sequence of intermediate chunk estimates becomes a formal progressive rate-distortion code: truncating the ODE at any NFE is guaranteed no worse than a single-shot model trained for that exact budget.
source_papers: Equitz & Cover — Successive Refinement of Information, IEEE T-IT 37(2):269-275, 1991
Rimoldi — Successive Refinement of Information, IEEE T-IT 1994
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency under a variable real-time compute budget, and long-horizon compounding error
candidates.mechanistic_story: A flow-matching sampler's intermediate ODE states already refine over NFE, but nothing in the standard objective guarantees early truncation is rate-distortion-optimal for that budget, so ad hoc early stopping degrades unpredictably. Enforcing the successive-refinability Markov condition at training turns the ODE trajectory into a real progressive code, giving latency-adaptive control with a formal quality bound, and lets the model allocate more capacity to near-term chunk steps — the ones dominating long-horizon compounding error.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: 'Denoising Tells When to Replan' (DVAC, arXiv:2606.03847) and related adaptive-chunking methods use the trained denoising trajectory as a TEST-TIME signal for when to replan — a heuristic read of a fixed model, not a training-time successive-refinability objective. Distinct from killed #3 (AR text-token continuation): PRC targets continuous ODE truncation for anytime compute. No paper found training a VLA head under an explicit successive-refinement constraint.
candidates.integration_path: Add a nested-distortion auxiliary loss across a small set of ODE truncation points (NFE in {1,2,4,8}) to the existing flow-matching loss, computed on intermediate ODE states already produced during training — same expert, same param count, no new inference params. At deployment the controller picks NFE per compute budget.
candidates.pre_flag: Replan-cadence/adaptive-compute cluster; cite DVAC — training-time objective vs test-time heuristic read is the delta.

candidates.name: CS-Head — Compressed-Sensing Action Head
candidates.mechanism: Parameterize the action chunk as a sparse code in a fixed/lightly-learned dictionary and have the head regress only M random-projection measurement coefficients (M ~ k log(n/k) per RIP theory) instead of the full n-dim chunk, reconstructing via a fixed L1 or small LISTA-unrolled decoder at inference.
source_papers: Candès & Tao — Decoding by Linear Programming, IEEE T-IT 2005
Donoho — Compressed Sensing, IEEE T-IT 2006
Candès, Romberg & Tao — Robust Uncertainty Principles, IEEE T-IT 2006
candidates.vla_bottleneck: few-shot data efficiency at 10-25 demos (explicitly flagged as largely uncharacterized)
candidates.mechanistic_story: CS theory guarantees exact/stable sparse-code recovery from M<<n incoherent random measurements when the signal is k-sparse; action chunks are smooth, structured, low-complexity trajectories, plausibly k-sparse in a simple dictionary. A head fitting only M measurement coefficients has far fewer effective parameters to learn from scarce demonstrations, and RIP/incoherence gives an explicit, falsifiable prediction of how many demos are needed before recovery is reliable — turning 'compact heads help at low data' into a theory-derived sample-complexity bound.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: FAST/BEAST/OmniSAT/VQ-VLA (crowded area) use fixed dictionary/DCT/spline/VQ compression, but none frame the head as a compressed-sensing measurement operator with an RIP/incoherence recovery guarantee tying demo count to sparsity. 'ActionCodec' (arXiv 2602.15397) analyzes tokenizer desiderata as static design, not a random-projection recovery-guarantee construction. No compressed-sensing VLA action-head found.
candidates.integration_path: Replace the output layer with a linear sensing layer producing M coefficients (sweep M=8-32) plus a small LISTA-style/fixed-L1 decoder (~1-3M params) reconstructing the full chunk at inference. Reuses the 10/25/50-demo few-shot protocol already planned.
candidates.pre_flag: Adjacent to crowded action-tokenizer/compact-head area (FAST/BEAST/VQ); differentiator is the RIP-based recovery-guarantee framing.

candidates.name: SynergyPrior: NMF-Derived Few-Shot Action Subspace Adapter
candidates.source_domain: biology — muscle synergies / motor primitive dimensionality
candidates.mechanism: From the K=10-25 demos of a few-shot task, factorize the action-chunk matrix with non-negative matrix factorization (as in EMG muscle-synergy extraction) into a small set of non-negative synergy vectors + time-varying activation coefficients. Freeze this per-task-family synergy basis and adapt only a tiny coefficient-prediction head on frozen VLM features, so few-shot learning fits a handful of non-negative activation weights per timestep instead of the full action-chunk manifold.
source_papers: d'Avella, Saltiel, Bizzi, Nature Neuroscience 2003
Cheung, d'Avella, Tresch, Bizzi, J. Neuroscience 2005
candidates.vla_bottleneck: few-shot data efficiency at 10-25 demos (named as largely uncharacterized)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Biological motor control avoids re-learning full activation patterns for every new movement by recombining a small individual-specific synergy basis; the CNS only tunes a few coefficients. Applied to few-shot VLA adaptation, a synergy basis extracted directly from the tiny target-task demo set (not a globally pretrained tokenizer) gives the adapter a much smaller effective output space exactly when data is scarcest.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: 'Discovering Synergies for Robot Manipulation with Multi-Task RL' (arXiv 2110.01530) discovers a synergy space for dexterous-hand RL — closest precedent, but RL-trained end-to-end (not a frozen-backbone imitation adapter), not VLA/language-conditioned, not few-shot, and predates VLA. No hit combining synergy extraction with a frozen VLA backbone or LIBERO few-shot.
candidates.integration_path: Offline per-task-family: NMF on the K-demo action-chunk tensor → synergy basis W (a few hundred params). Online: small MLP (pooled frozen-VLM feature → non-negative coefficients, ReLU/softmax-gated, tens of thousands of params) trained on the K demos; final action = W @ coefficients. Trains in minutes.
candidates.pre_flag: Close to the crowded compact-output-head territory (BEAST/B-spline); differentiator is the non-negative, demo-covariance-derived (not globally pretrained) basis — argue explicitly.

candidates.name: BucketGate (Token-Bucket Subgoal Admission Control)
candidates.mechanism: Treat each candidate subgoal transition as a packet requesting admission. A token bucket accumulates confidence tokens at a steady rate from a lightweight completion-confidence head; a transition is admitted only once accumulated tokens clear a threshold (sustained multi-timestep evidence), with burst capacity allowing fast admission when evidence is overwhelming but capping how fast transitions can chain, preventing cascading premature transitions.
source_papers: Turner, 'New Directions in Communications', IEEE Comm. Mag. 1986 (ATM token-bucket)
Guerin, Ahmadi, Naghshineh, 'Equivalent Capacity ...', IEEE JSAC 9(7), 1991
candidates.vla_bottleneck: long-horizon failure (SmolVLA 49-71% on LIBERO-Long vs 94%+ OFT-7B) from cascading premature/missed subgoal transitions
candidates.mechanistic_story: Long-horizon collapse is often a chain-of-errors problem: one premature transition propagates downstream. A token bucket admits a transition only after evidence has accumulated past a rate-limited budget, giving hysteresis against noisy single-frame confidence spikes while still permitting fast admission when evidence is unambiguous — the mechanism ATM networks use to smooth bursty traffic while bounding worst-case admission rate.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: SeqVLA (arXiv:2509.14138, completion-detection head for pi0) and StreamVLA (arXiv:2602.01100, 'Lock-and-Gated' completion-state gating) add a learned completion signal but gate on the instantaneous/lightly-filtered detector output, not a formally rate-bounded, burst-tolerant token reservoir. Delta is the debouncing/rate-limiting mechanism, not the general idea of completion gating.
candidates.integration_path: One extra scalar (token count) in the LIBERO-Long rollout loop plus a ~50K-param MLP completion-confidence head trained on frozen features (same recipe as SeqVLA's detection head). Two tuned hyperparameters (fill rate, bucket size). No backbone gradients.
candidates.pre_flag: Subtask-transition cluster (C25/C20/C16/C46/C40); overlaps SeqVLA/StreamVLA completion gating — differentiator is only the rate-limiting mechanism.

candidates.name: Kinematic Address-Prefetch for Vision Encoding
candidates.mechanism: Once the flow-matching head commits an action chunk, the robot's future end-effector pose for the next K steps is known deterministically (forward kinematics) — an address, not a value, prediction. A lightweight predictor uses that known future pose plus recent optical-flow/attention history to pick the camera crop/region SmolVLM2's SigLIP tower will need next, and starts patch-embedding + early transformer blocks for that region on a separate CUDA stream while the cheap flow-matching ODE for the current chunk is still running — so vision features are warm when the real frame arrives.
source_papers: SPPAM: Signature Pattern Prediction and Access-Map Prefetcher (arXiv:2602.04100)
ICP: Instruction-Correlation Prefetching (arXiv:2605.15645)
Toward Intelligent Prefetching: A Survey (arXiv:2606.09955)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency/compute — the vision tower forward is the largest single latency item in the control loop
candidates.mechanistic_story: Prefetching works because address prediction is far cheaper than the fetch; here region prediction (an MLP over known-future pose + attention history) is far cheaper than the SigLIP forward it precomputes. Overlapping that forward with the current chunk's cheap denoising converts backbone latency from 'on the critical path every chunk' to 'hidden behind compute that was happening anyway'.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: F2F-AP (arXiv:2604.02408), AsyncVLA (arXiv:2602.13476), DEFLECT (arXiv:2605.19294), Speculative Policy Orchestration (arXiv:2603.19418) address the observation-execution latency gap by training the policy to tolerate/correct staleness or by using a generative world model to hallucinate frames. None do non-generative, address-only speculative precompute of encoder compute keyed off the committed chunk's known kinematics.
candidates.integration_path: Wrapper ahead of the SmolVLA vision connector: a ~1-5M param MLP/GRU region predictor consumes the committed chunk (already in the buffer) + last N attention maps, outputs a crop/priority mask; SigLIP's patch embed + first few blocks run on that crop on a background CUDA stream during ODE integration, finalized once the true frame lands. Only the predictor is trained (supervised on logged attention/crop-utility). Under a day.
candidates.pre_flag: Latency-hiding/pipeline-scheduling tag (C47/C48); adjacent to crowded speculative-decoding-for-VLA — differentiator is address-only (non-generative) encoder precompute.

candidates.name: Subtask Branch Predictor with Speculative Squash
candidates.mechanism: Treat each subtask transition (pick→place→pick→place in LIBERO-Long) as a branch. A small history-indexed predictor forecasts the top-2 likely next subtasks before the current one is confirmed complete; because the flow-matching expert is cheap relative to the frozen backbone, both candidate branches' action chunks are computed in parallel off a single shared backbone forward (different conditioning/goal tokens), and once a lightweight completion detector resolves which subtask finished, the correct chunk is committed instantly and the other is squashed.
source_papers: Yeh & Patt (1991), 'Two-Level Adaptive Training Branch Prediction', MICRO-24
Jimenez & Lin (2001), 'Dynamic Branch Prediction with Perceptrons', HPCA-7
candidates.vla_bottleneck: long-horizon (SmolVLA 49-71% on LIBERO-Long vs 94%+); phase-transition latency and misidentified-subtask errors compound in this regime
candidates.mechanistic_story: In long-horizon tasks the dominant latency/error cost is at subtask boundaries: the model must notice completion, then pay a full backbone-conditioning cycle before the next subtask's actions are ready, and a misjudged transition compounds downstream. Precomputing the likely next branch removes that cold-start gap at the transition (branch resolved → zero added backbone latency) the way branch prediction removes pipeline bubbles at control-flow changes.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: SeqVLA (arXiv:2509.14138), LoHo-Manip/trace-conditioned planning (arXiv:2604.21924), StreamVLA (arXiv:2602.01100), Speculative Verification for VLA (arXiv:2604.02965) all detect/verify a SINGLE current-plan hypothesis; none maintain and speculatively compute multiple candidate next-subtask branches in parallel with squash-on-resolve.
candidates.integration_path: A ~1-3M param history-table predictor (keyed on recent action-entropy trace + language/goal embedding) alongside the flow-matching head; reuses one backbone forward per chunk but reruns the small expert twice with different goal conditioning for the top-2 branches. Needs a completion/transition detector trained on LIBERO's compositional subtask boundaries. Backbone frozen; under a day.
candidates.pre_flag: Subtask-transition + latency-hiding clusters; adjacent to crowded speculative-decoding-for-VLA.

candidates.name: VisionBP (Backpressure-Gated Perception)
candidates.mechanism: Model the action-execution buffer (queue of not-yet-executed actions from the last chunk) as a queue with occupancy Q. The vision encoder only runs a new expensive backbone forward pass when Q drops below a threshold (buffer draining) or an urgent interrupt fires (large frame-difference norm indicating scene change); otherwise cached visual tokens/actions are reused. Literal Tassiulas-Ephremides backpressure: upstream transmission (backbone compute) is throttled by downstream queue backlog, not a fixed clock.
source_papers: Tassiulas & Ephremides, 'Stability properties of constrained queueing systems ...', IEEE CDC 1990 (extended IEEE TAC 1992)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency and compute efficiency (backbone dominates) while avoiding stale actions during fast scene changes (robustness)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Backbone compute is currently spent on a fixed schedule independent of whether the queued actions are still valid. Tying backbone invocation to actual queue starvation spends compute exactly when needed, the principle that gives backpressure routing maximum-throughput stability — plus the urgent-interrupt path recovers robustness to scene changes a fixed clock would miss.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Asynchronous fast-slow VLA producer-consumer buffers (arXiv 2512.20188) decouple inference/execution via a buffer, but re-inference is driven by wall-clock/thread scheduling, not an explicit backpressure control law coupling queue occupancy to upstream admission. Distinct from killed #3 (AR continuation).
candidates.integration_path: Wrap the rollout loop's action-queue check (lerobot already tracks queue length) with a threshold + frame-diff interrupt; zero new trainable params for the basic version, optional ~1K-param threshold-tuning head. No backbone changes.
candidates.pre_flag: Replan-cadence cluster (C20/C31/C42/C43/C51/C52/C29): control-law gating of backbone invocation; sibling of C51 (AIMD).

candidates.name: Attention-Guided Occlusion Training
candidates.mechanism: Reuse the pooled cross-attention importance scoring from SnapKV/H2O — normally used to decide which KV entries to evict at inference — purely as a training-time signal: periodically identify the highest-importance vision token(s) for the current batch and mask/zero them for a fraction of training steps, forcing the action expert to not collapse its evidence onto one or two visual tokens.
source_papers: arXiv 2306.14048 (Zhang et al., H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle)
arXiv 2404.14469 (Li et al., SnapKV)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: robustness to distractors/viewpoint (LIBERO-Plus) and few-shot data efficiency (a free, targeted augmentation requiring no additional demonstrations)
candidates.mechanistic_story: If the policy's cross-attention already concentrates on a small set of tokens (the phenomenon SnapKV/H2O exploit for compression), those tokens are exactly the single point of failure that camera shift, lighting change, or an added distractor will corrupt. Training-time occlusion of the model's own top-attention tokens is a targeted, mechanism-aware analogue of dropout/cutout that directly attacks over-reliance rather than random pixels.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: VLA-Cache (2502.02175), VLA-Pruner (2511.16449), SP-VLA (2506.12723), AURA (2606.02775), OxyGen (2603.14371) all use related attention-importance scores, but every one applies the score at INFERENCE time to evict/reuse KV entries for latency/memory, never as a TRAINING-time robustness augmentation with zero inference-time cost. Scanner flags this as the thinnest-differentiation idea in its set.
candidates.integration_path: Pure training-time procedure: compute pooled attention scores over a calibration sub-batch every N steps, mask top-scoring vision tokens for a random subset of examples, otherwise unchanged forward/backward. Zero added parameters, zero added inference cost, frozen-backbone compatible.
candidates.pre_flag: Scanner self-flags thin differentiation vs a very crowded KV-importance area; novelty-audit should scrutinize whether training-time-vs-inference-time is a sufficient delta.

candidates.name: Flow-AIMD (Congestion-Controlled Replan Cadence)
candidates.mechanism: Maintain a persistent congestion window W = number of action-chunk steps to execute open-loop before the next VLM+flow-matching forward pass. After each sub-chunk, a tiny (~10K-param) MLP reads cheap already-available signals (proprio tracking residual, disagreement across flow-matching ODE seeds) and outputs a risk scalar. Clean signal → additive increase W+=1 (coast longer); risky → multiplicative decrease W/=2 (replan fast). Stateful across the whole episode, unlike a per-chunk threshold.
source_papers: Chiu & Jain, 'Analysis of the Increase and Decrease Algorithms for Congestion Avoidance', Computer Networks 17:1-14, 1989
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency/compute (backbone dominates) and robustness collapse under perturbation (LIBERO-Plus)
candidates.mechanistic_story: SmolVLA re-invokes the full backbone on a fixed schedule regardless of scene difficulty. An AIMD feedback controller lets the policy stretch open-loop execution during stable segments and clamp down hard the instant a risk signal fires — the throughput-vs-loss tradeoff TCP solves for network links, applied to the staleness-vs-compute tradeoff of an action chunk, with formal convergence properties a memoryless threshold lacks.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: DVAC (arXiv 2606.03847) is closest — a memoryless per-chunk variance threshold, not a stateful multiplicative-backoff/additive-increase controller with persistent window. Distinct from killed #3 (RTC AR continuation) since it sits on top of ordinary flow-matching chunk execution.
candidates.integration_path: Add to the lerobot rollout loop around select_action/chunk generation: one scalar W as loop state, one ~10K-param MLP risk estimator trained in minutes on rollout logs. No backbone/expert weight changes.
candidates.pre_flag: Replan-cadence cluster (C20/C31/C42/C43/C51/C52/C29); sibling of C49 (backpressure) and C20 (funnel) — competing control laws for the same trigger.

candidates.name: Snapshot-Isolated Action Commit (OCC-VLA)
candidates.mechanism: Treat each action-chunk generation as an optimistic transaction: record the read-set (the observation-token snapshot the denoiser conditioned on) alongside the generated chunk. Before committing each action, cheaply diff the current live observation against the recorded read-set (pooled-feature distance, no model call); on divergence past a calibrated threshold mid-chunk, abort the remaining suffix and re-run generation from the fresh snapshot — OCC's read-set validation, not a fixed-latency compensator.
source_papers: Bernstein & Goodman, 'Concurrency Control in Distributed Database Systems', ACM Comp. Surveys 13(2), 1981
Berenson et al., 'A Critique of ANSI SQL Isolation Levels', SIGMOD 1995
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency-induced staleness during open-loop action-chunk execution, and its knock-on robustness cost
candidates.mechanistic_story: Backbone inference is slow relative to control rate, so SmolVLA commits to a whole chunk from one stale observation and executes open-loop; if the world changes mid-chunk it has no mechanism to notice. OCC's read-set/validate-before-commit protocol gives an explicit, cheap conflict-detection step per action, turning staleness into a detectable, correctable event — directly attacking the blind multi-step execution window the handoff notes flag as a likely SmolVLA failure mode.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Asynchronous fast-slow decoupling (DuoCore-FS, arXiv 2512.20188) and delay-aware smoothing (Action ControlNet, arXiv 2606.25985) address staleness architecturally but neither records an explicit read-set nor performs threshold-based conflict validation with selective abort-and-regenerate.
candidates.integration_path: Wrap SmolVLAPolicy.select_action/predict_action_chunk: cache the pooled feature used to condition the current sample as the read-set; each step compares its fresh pooled feature against the cached read-set via cosine/L2 (a few FLOPs, no model call); above threshold, discard queued actions and re-invoke the frozen expert on the fresh observation. Zero new params beyond a calibrated threshold.
candidates.pre_flag: Replan-cadence cluster (C20/C31/C42/C43/C51/C52/C29): observation-drift-triggered replan; differentiator vs C20/C29 is read-set feature divergence rather than tracking error.

candidates.name: Scoreboard-Gated Asynchronous Modality Issue
candidates.mechanism: A scoreboard tracks per-source (vision, language, proprioception) freshness/ready bits and lets the ODE integrator issue its early denoising steps against already-ready sources, stalling only the specific step that first cross-attends to the still-in-flight vision features — instead of SmolVLA's current synchronous barrier where all encoders must finish before any denoising begins, even though proprioception is near-instant and language is often cached across an episode.
source_papers: Thornton, J.E. (1964), 'Parallel Operation in the Control Data 6600', AFIPS FJCC
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency/compute — a coarse all-or-nothing sync barrier wastes the interval where cheap modalities are ready but the expensive one is not
candidates.mechanistic_story: A blanket barrier synchronizes on the slowest source every chunk even though only some denoising steps depend on it; fine-grained hazard tracking converts that fixed wait into a data-dependency-scoped wait, so the achievable control-loop period tracks the true critical path of the current chunk's cross-attention pattern instead of the backbone's worst-case latency — a pure scheduling change with no backbone gradients.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: F2F-AP (arXiv:2604.02408) and the Latency-Aware Framework for Visuomotor Policy Learning (arXiv:2602.14255) schedule already-computed action chunks against real-world clock time between inference calls (inter-chunk); neither tracks per-modality data dependencies WITHIN a single forward pass to let denoising issue before every encoder has returned.
candidates.integration_path: A thin scheduler (<1M params, a small learned or rule-based per-source latency/dependency table) inserted into SmolVLAPolicy.forward/sample_actions between the three encoders and the flow-matching integrator, requiring encoders dispatched as separate async calls and the ODE loop to declare per step which source it cross-attends to. A refactor of the forward path plus the small scheduler; tunable in under a day.
candidates.pre_flag: Latency-hiding/pipeline-scheduling tag (C47/C48/C53).

candidates.name: Bandit-Gated Execution Modes (Bao-VLA)
candidates.source_domain: databases — learned query optimization / cost models
candidates.mechanism: Train a small contextual bandit 'hint selector' (Thompson sampling over a handful of arms, as in Bao) that, per observation, picks among a small fixed menu of qualitatively different execution modes (chunk_size in {8, 50}, or flow-matching vs L1-head decode) rather than scoring many stochastic samples of the same type. Carries Bao's core trick: arm 0 is always the current shipped-default behavior, and the bandit is regret-bounded so it provably falls back to that default whenever confidence is low.
source_papers: Marcus et al., 'Bao: Making Learned Query Optimization Practical', SIGMOD 2021 (Best Paper)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency/compute at precision-critical vs free-space moments, and long-horizon failure from a one-size-fits-all fixed chunk size
candidates.mechanistic_story: SmolVLA uses one fixed chunk_size=50 for the whole episode; long-horizon tasks fail disproportionately at contact-rich sub-moments where a long open-loop chunk overshoots, while free-space transit pays full decode cost for no reason. A regret-bounded bandit switching among a small discrete menu gets the compute/latency win of short-chunk precision only when needed, with a hard safety guarantee (never much worse than the shipped baseline) that heuristic entropy-based adaptive-chunking lacks.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Adaptive action-chunk-size methods are a crowded adjacent area: HiPolicy (arXiv 2604.06067), Adaptive Action Chunking at Inference-time (arXiv 2604.04161), Adaptive Q-Chunking (arXiv 2605.05544) — all pick chunk size via a learned heuristic/critic, none carry a formal regret-bounded bandit with a mandatory safe-default fallback in the Bao sense. Closest hit HiPolicy/AAC overlaps clearly.
candidates.integration_path: A ~50K-param bandit head reads a lightweight feature of the pooled embedding + proprioception, outputs an arm among {chunk_size=50 flow default, chunk_size=8 flow, chunk_size=1 L1 fallback} before each action-expert call; trained via Thompson sampling on rollout return with a hard epsilon-floor on the default arm. Inference-time module only.
candidates.pre_flag: Replan-cadence / crowded adaptive-chunking cluster (HiPolicy/AAC); novelty must be framed narrowly around the safe-fallback/regret-bound, not 'adaptive chunk size' itself.

candidates.name: Workload View-Selection Skill Cache
candidates.mechanism: Borrow the view-selection formulation (a lattice of candidate derived computations, each with benefit = query-frequency-weighted savings and cost = storage + incremental-maintenance overhead) to decide, at the level of the task/instruction WORKLOAD across many episodes, which intermediate language-conditioned subgoal representations are worth persistently caching vs recomputing from the frozen backbone. A small greedy/ILP selector picks the materialization set under a fixed budget, re-solving as the instruction-frequency distribution shifts.
source_papers: Harinarayan, Rajaraman, Ullman, 'Implementing Data Cubes Efficiently', SIGMOD 1996
'Workload acceleration by optimizing materialized view selection using local search', 2026
candidates.vla_bottleneck: compute efficiency / backbone-dominated latency across a task distribution, without touching frozen weights
candidates.mechanistic_story: The frozen backbone dominates inference cost, so the only lever for compute efficiency is deciding what NOT to recompute. Existing VLA caching reuses computation WITHIN one rollout via recency/frequency heuristics. A workload-level view-selection formulation instead asks which language-conditioned intermediate computations pay for their storage/maintenance cost often enough across the actual skewed instruction distribution to persist across episodes — a benefit-vs-maintenance-cost optimization rather than an LRU/frequency heuristic, landing on a better Pareto point because it accounts for maintenance cost recency caching ignores.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: VLA-Cache (arXiv 2502.02175), RoboMME (arXiv 2603.04639), ReCache (arXiv 2606.06060) are all within-episode recency/frequency-driven reuse, not a cross-episode workload-level cost-benefit selection with an explicit incremental-maintenance term. No workload/view-selection formulation found for VLA.
candidates.integration_path: A selector alongside the SmolVLA language-conditioning path: log the distribution of instruction embeddings, build a candidate lattice of intermediate conditioning vectors, run greedy/ILP selection offline on the logged workload to choose a fixed cache of size B, and route matching instructions to the cached vector at inference (skipping the frozen backbone's language-conditioning forward for hits). Optional ~1M-param similarity-matching head; no new backbone params.
candidates.pre_flag: Adjacent to crowded KV-cache-reuse / VLA caching area; differentiator is cross-episode workload cost-benefit vs within-episode recency.

candidates.name: Step-Recurrent Flow Head (Linear-Recurrent State Across ODE Denoising Steps)
candidates.mechanism: Instead of running ~10 independent full cross-attention passes (one per flow-matching integration step) each re-attending to the same frozen VLM context from scratch, thread a small SSM/linear-attention recurrent state through the denoising trajectory: each step updates a compact hidden state in linear time and only a cheap linear read-out re-derives the velocity field, rather than a full quadratic cross-attention recomputation every step.
source_papers: arXiv 2312.00752 (Gu & Dao, Mamba)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: latency — the flow-matching expert's cost scales with the number of ODE integration steps, each paying full cross-attention cost against the cached context
candidates.mechanistic_story: The ~10 denoising steps are a short, highly redundant sequence (each step's velocity prediction is close to the previous one); an SSM's linear-time recurrence is a natural fit for compressing that redundancy into a carried state instead of paying full attention cost every step — the efficiency argument Mamba makes for long token sequences, applied to the denoising-step sequence rather than the spatial/token sequence.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: FlowRAM (arXiv:2506.16201) and SpatialVLA-Mamba both combine Mamba with flow-matching, but they replace the action decoder's spatial/token processing with an SSM; they do not restructure computation across the DENOISING-STEP axis itself while leaving the per-step token architecture intact. This is the closest and most direct overlap.
candidates.integration_path: Replace the repeated per-step cross-attention block in the action expert with a small SSM layer whose state persists across the ~10 integration calls within one control-step's flow solve (reset each new observation); everything remains inside the trainable action expert, no backbone gradients.
candidates.pre_flag: FlowRAM/SpatialVLA-Mamba are close (Mamba+flow-matching); differentiator is the denoising-step axis, which the audit should verify is genuinely untouched by those works.

candidates.name: CriticalInit: Edge-of-Chaos Initialization for the Action Expert's Temporal Memory
candidates.mechanism: Whatever small recurrent/state-tracking component the action expert uses to carry information across chunk boundaries (e.g. a lightweight GRU/SSM memory bolted onto the flow-matching head to track task progress), initialize and constrain its recurrent weight spectral radius near the critical value rather than standard orthogonal/Xavier init, and monitor it during training to stay near criticality (a regularizer term, not a backbone change).
source_papers: Bertschinger & Natschlager, 'Real-Time Computation at the Edge of Chaos in RNNs', Neural Computation 2004
Legenstein & Maass, 'Edge of chaos and prediction of computational performance', Neural Networks 2007
candidates.vla_bottleneck: long-horizon collapse and robustness/generalization (criticality is empirically linked to maximized memory capacity and generalization)
candidates.mechanistic_story: Recurrent systems initialized deep in the ordered regime forget too fast (poor long-horizon memory); deep in the chaotic regime they amplify noise (poor robustness). The edge-of-chaos point jointly maximizes memory capacity and dynamic range — a near-zero-cost initialization/regularization choice that plausibly helps exactly the two named weak points of small VLA long-horizon tracking.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: None found applying edge-of-chaos/criticality tuning to any VLA component. General 'edge of chaos as guiding principle for NN training' work exists for generic classifiers/RL, not robotics/VLA.
candidates.integration_path: Applies only to a recurrent/state-tracking module that would need to exist anyway for a long-horizon memory experiment (e.g. a small GRU auxiliary to the flow head, tens of thousands of params). Spectral-radius rescaling at init is one line; a soft criticality regularizer adds negligible cost.
candidates.pre_flag: Scanner itself says best framed as an ablation/add-on layered onto another candidate (e.g. C18 ReservoirAct or a long-horizon memory module), NOT a standalone paper — demoted accordingly despite high raw novelty.

candidates.name: Facility-Location Demo Coreset
candidates.mechanism: Before few-shot finetuning at a fixed demo budget K (10/25), run k-center-greedy coreset selection over frozen-backbone embeddings of a larger candidate demo pool to pick the K most diverse/representative trajectories, replacing the field's default random or first-K selection, maximizing embedding-space coverage under the fixed labeling budget.
source_papers: Sener & Savarese, 'Active Learning for CNNs: A Core-Set Approach', ICLR 2018 (arXiv:1708.00489)
candidates.vla_bottleneck: few-shot data efficiency at 10-25 demos — the project's own report names the few-shot crossover as its single load-bearing open axis
candidates.mechanistic_story: At K=10-25 demos, which demos you get matters as much as which head you use: a random draw can by chance omit a whole manipulation phase (a failed-grasp recovery, a particular object pose), starving compact heads of exactly the coverage they need. Diversity-maximizing coreset selection over the already-cached backbone embeddings targets that coverage gap for near-zero extra compute, orthogonal to and composable with the planned head atlas. Data selection under a fixed budget, not data scaling.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Demo-SCORE (arXiv:2503.03707, WebFetch-verified) filters a large heterogeneous dataset POST-HOC using a classifier trained on the policy's own online rollout successes, requiring the policy to already be running and a large pool; not upfront coreset selection under a fixed small budget with zero online-rollout requirement. 'Efficient In-context Demonstration Selection with Coreset' (arXiv:2511.08977) applies coreset to in-context prompting for LVLMs, not physical demonstrations for IL finetuning.
candidates.integration_path: Standalone pre-processing script run once per task: mean-pool the frozen features already cached by backbone.py, run greedy k-center to pick K trajectories, feed that subset into the existing shot10/shot25 loops unchanged. Zero new params, minutes on CPU/GPU using cached embeddings — cheapest idea to pilot.

candidates.name: Query-Cracked Few-Shot Memory
candidates.mechanism: Instead of building a full nearest-neighbor/cluster index over demonstration embeddings upfront or re-indexing wholesale as new demos arrive, apply the cracking principle: each retrieval query (an incoming instruction, or a new streamed demo) partially reorganizes the memory in place — the structure is never separately 'built', only refined as a byproduct of retrievals issued — so cost is paid only for regions of instruction-space actually queried, converging to a fine partition where deployment traffic concentrates and staying coarse elsewhere.
source_papers: Idreos, Kersten, Manegold, 'Database Cracking', CIDR 2007
Idreos et al., 'Merging What's Cracked ...', VLDB 2011
candidates.vla_bottleneck: few-shot data efficiency at 10-25 demos, specifically the amortized cost of keeping a retrieval-based few-shot memory current online
candidates.mechanistic_story: In the ≤25-demo regime, a full re-embed/re-cluster of a retrieval memory after every new demo is disproportionately expensive relative to the new data. Cracking's guarantee — reorganization cost proportional to queries actually issued, never a full rebuild — means a streamed few-shot loop pays near-zero upfront indexing tax and gets progressively cheaper and more accurate retrieval for recurring instruction patterns, the opposite of a static offline-built index.
candidates.nearest_vla_prior_art: Most crowded of its set. Retrieval-augmented few-shot/continual robot learning is active: STRAP (2412.15182), ROSER (2603.01474, explicitly 'efficiently indexing new data as it becomes available' for continual few-shot), Retrieve-then-Steer (2605.10094), TOPIC/FSAIL (2504.15517), Retrieve-Reason-Act (2603.02688). ROSER is functionally adjacent. The cracking distinction (reorg strictly as a side-effect of retrieval reads, workload-adaptive granularity) was not found verbatim but the surrounding territory is dense — a differentiator on an existing idea, not a clean gap.
candidates.integration_path: Replace a conventional FAISS/kNN index over demo embeddings (auxiliary few-shot conditioning for the language input) with a cracked column-store-style array: on each retrieval, partition the queried region around the query embedding (O(log n) partial sort), so the structure is exact only where queries touched it. A few hundred lines; no new trainable params — a systems-layer change.
candidates.pre_flag: Hard pre-flag: most-crowded retrieval-augmented-few-shot area (ROSER functionally adjacent); scanner says not a clean gap. Ranked last; novelty-audit likely decides its fate.
